issues.title: Add API-compat tooling: public API breaks are shipping unnoticed in patch/minor releases
issues.body:
## Problem

Nothing in this repo detects a public API break. `CLAUDE.md` sets a clear contract:

> **No breaking changes** to public API without a major version bump (semver)
> Breaking = removing/renaming public classes, functions, or parameters; changing return types; reordering non-named parameters; changing enum/sealed-class variants consumers may match on
> Deprecate before removing — add `@Deprecated` with `ReplaceWith` and keep for at least one minor release before removal

That contract is currently enforced by review alone, and an audit of the release history shows it has been missed repeatedly. `@Deprecated` has **never appeared** in `musicmeta-core/src/main/` in this repo's history — every removal so far skipped the deprecation cycle.

## How it surfaced

The `demo/` composite build stopped compiling:

```
e: DemoCommands.kt:137:93 Argument type mismatch: actual type is 'Set<EnrichmentType>',
   but 'EnrichmentIdentifiers?' was expected.
```

Commit 4b3f08a inserted `identifiers: EnrichmentIdentifiers? = null` into the **middle** of the parameter list of `artistProfile` / `albumProfile` / `trackProfile` in `EnrichmentEngineExtensions.kt`, between `mbid` and `types`. Every positional argument after `mbid` shifts one slot left. It shipped in **v0.9.2 — a patch release**.

## Audit findings

The demo break is not isolated. Across the tag history:

**Mid-list parameter insertions** (break positional callers)
| Symbol | File | Commit | Shipped | Bump |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `artistProfile`/`albumProfile`/`trackProfile` — `identifiers` | `EnrichmentEngineExtensions.kt` | 4b3f08a | v0.9.2 | patch |
| `EnrichmentConfig.radioDiscoveryMode` | `EnrichmentConfig.kt` | 6bdb7c3 | v0.9.0 | minor |
| `EnrichmentData.Metadata.genreTags` | `EnrichmentData.kt` | 4640dc8 | v0.5.0 | minor |
| `EnrichmentCacheEntity` — 3 params | `android/cache/EnrichmentCacheEntity.kt` | b32d7d1 | v0.7.0 | minor |

`Metadata` is `@Serializable`, so that one also shifted kotlinx serialization element indices. CHANGELOG describes it as "backward-compatible alongside existing `genres` field".

**Removed / renamed with no deprecation period**
- `EnrichmentConfig.preferredArtworkSize` + `DEFAULT_ARTWORK_SIZE` deleted — 312e6c8, v0.4.0. Not in CHANGELOG at all.
- `EnrichmentData.IdentifierResolution` sealed variant deleted — 99e3868, v0.4.0.
- `ProviderCapability.requiresIdentifier: Boolean` → `identifierRequirement: IdentifierRequirement` — 957004a, v0.4.0. Breaks every third-party provider implementation.
- `SimilarArtist.musicBrainzId` / `PopularTrack.musicBrainzId` → `identifiers: EnrichmentIdentifiers` — cbda960, v0.4.0. Both `@Serializable`, so persisted JSON breaks too.

**Return type / interface changes** (these two *were* flagged in CHANGELOG, though under `### Changed` rather than the `### Breaking Changes` heading CLAUDE.md requires)
- `EnrichmentEngine.enrich()` → `EnrichmentResults` instead of `Map<...>` — b32d7d1, v0.7.0.
- `EnrichmentEngine` gained `invalidate()` / `isManuallySelected()` / `markManuallySelected()` with no default bodies — b32d7d1, v0.7.0.

**Enum entries inserted mid-list** (ordinal shifts; lower severity since the Room cache persists `type.name`, not ordinals) — `ErrorKind.TIMEOUT` before `UNKNOWN`, and `EnrichmentType` entries in v0.4.0, v0.5.0, v0.7.0, v0.9.0.

Clean releases, for contrast: v0.5.0→v0.6.0 and v0.7.0→v0.8.0 were purely additive (params appended with defaults, interface methods with default bodies). v0.8.0→v0.8.1, v0.8.1→v0.8.2, v0.9.0→v0.9.1 had zero public API diff. So the good pattern is already well understood — it just isn't enforced.

## Proposal

Adopt Kotlin's [`binary-compatibility-validator`](https://github.com/Kotlin/binary-compatibility-validator). It dumps the public ABI to a committed `.api` file and fails the build when the current API diverges from it — the same **baseline-lock tripwire** shape as `image-drift.yml` in MediaStack-private, where `docs/operations/image-digests.lock` is the tested baseline and drift is surfaced rather than silently tolerated.

1. Apply the plugin at the root, enable for `musicmeta-core`, `musicmeta-android`, `musicmeta-okhttp`.
2. `./gradlew apiDump` once to generate the baselines; commit them.
3. Wire `apiCheck` into the PR gate (see the test-CI issue) so a diverging signature blocks merge.
4. Reviewing an intentional break becomes reviewing the `.api` diff — the change is explicit in the PR rather than inferred from the source diff.

Optionally mirror the drift-warn half of `image-drift.yml`: a scheduled job that files/updates a single issue and auto-closes it once resolved, rather than just turning a run red.

## Scope of this issue

Part of #7.

**In scope**

1. Apply the plugin at the root; enable for `musicmeta-core`, `musicmeta-android`, `musicmeta-okhttp`.
2. `./gradlew apiDump` once to generate the baselines; commit them. Baselines record the API **as it
   actually stands at v0.9.2**, including the ~90 declarations under `provider/` and `http/` that the
   docs treat as internal but which are public in the ABI — see #5.
3. Add `apiCheck` to `.github/workflows/publish.yml`. That workflow runs
   `:musicmeta-core:test :musicmeta-okhttp:test` — not `build`, not `check` — so without this the only
   automated path to Maven Central would gain no gate at all.
4. Fix the positional call sites: `demo/DemoCommands.kt` lines 137/141 (see the comment below), and
   also the `SearchCandidate` overloads in `EnrichmentEngineExtensions.kt`, which pass `types` /
   `forceRefresh` positionally after a named `identifiers =` and compile today only because `types`
   still happens to land in slot 4. `demo/` was **not** the only positional consumer in the tree.

**Moved out**

- *PR-time gate* → **#3**, whose proposal already specifies all three jobs verbatim (`./gradlew build`,
  the `demo/` canary compile, `apiCheck`). No separate issue is needed.
- *The three follow-up decisions* (correct or document the v0.9.2 break, backfill `### Breaking
  Changes`, settle the 0.x semver stance) → **#4**.
- *Narrowing the public surface so "may change freely" is true* → **#5**.
- *Optional scheduled drift-warn job* → **#6**.

---

Branch: `ci/2`
comments:
## In scope: the `demo/` compile fix that exposed this

The break that surfaced this issue needs fixing as part of it. `demo/` no longer compiles against
`musicmeta-core` because commit 4b3f08a shifted the positional arguments:

```
e: DemoCommands.kt:137:93 Argument type mismatch: actual type is 'Set<EnrichmentType>',
   but 'EnrichmentIdentifiers?' was expected.
e: DemoCommands.kt:141:109 Argument type mismatch: actual type is 'Set<EnrichmentType>',
   but 'EnrichmentIdentifiers?' was expected.
```

The fix is to name the arguments so the call sites stop depending on position:

```diff
--- a/demo/src/main/kotlin/com/landofoz/musicmeta/demo/DemoCommands.kt
+++ b/demo/src/main/kotlin/com/landofoz/musicmeta/demo/DemoCommands.kt
@@ -134,11 +134,11 @@ internal suspend fun enrichProfile(
     is EnrichmentRequest.ForArtist -> {
-        val p = state.engine.artistProfile(request.name, request.identifiers.musicBrainzId, types, forceRefresh)
+        val p = state.engine.artistProfile(request.name, request.identifiers.musicBrainzId, types = types, forceRefresh = forceRefresh)
         EnrichedProfile.Artist(p)
     }
     is EnrichmentRequest.ForAlbum -> {
-        val p = state.engine.albumProfile(request.title, request.artist, request.identifiers.musicBrainzId, types, forceRefresh)
+        val p = state.engine.albumProfile(request.title, request.artist, request.identifiers.musicBrainzId, types = types, forceRefresh = forceRefresh)
         EnrichedProfile.Album(p)
     }
```

Verified: `cd demo && ../gradlew compileKotlin` succeeds with this applied.

`ForTrack` at line 145 needs no change — it already used named arguments, which is exactly why it
survived the shift. That contrast is the argument for naming arguments at every call site here.

### Why this belongs to this issue rather than a standalone fix

`demo/` is the only positional consumer of the profile extensions in the tree, which makes it the
repo's de facto API-compatibility canary — and nothing builds it. It is a separate composite build
(`includeBuild("..")`) and is not in `settings.gradle.kts`, so `./gradlew build` never compiles it.
Fixing the call sites without also wiring the canary into CI just removes the warning light.

So this issue should land three things together:

1. `binary-compatibility-validator` + committed `.api` baselines
2. `apiCheck` in the PR gate (depends on #3)
3. This demo fix, plus `cd demo && ../gradlew compileKotlin` as a CI step

Item 3 is captured in `docs/agent-workflows/conventions.md` §6 as the "positional-caller canary" row
of the verification surface.

issues.title: Add test CI on push/PR — tests currently run only at publish time, on an already-cut tag
issues.body:
## Problem

There is no CI on push or pull request. `.github/workflows/` contains exactly one workflow, `publish.yml`, and it triggers only on tags:

```yaml
on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'v*'
```

So the test suite runs **after** a release tag is cut, as a step inside the publish job. A regression is therefore discovered at publish time, on a tag that already exists, rather than on the PR that introduced it. Every commit between tags is unverified by CI.

## What this let through

The `demo/` composite build stopped compiling against `musicmeta-core` and nothing noticed. `demo/` is not in `settings.gradle.kts` — it is a separate build that pulls the library in via `includeBuild("..")` — so `./gradlew build` never compiles it. It is also the only positional consumer of the profile extension functions in the tree, which makes it an accidental but genuine API-compatibility canary. Nothing builds it.

Coverage gaps in the current setup:

- **No PR gate at all** — nothing blocks merging a commit that fails to compile or fails tests.
- **`demo/` never built** — not by `./gradlew build`, not by `publish.yml`.
- **`:musicmeta-android:test` never run in CI** — `publish.yml` runs only `:musicmeta-core:test :musicmeta-okhttp:test`. The android module (Room, Hilt, Robolectric, 13 tests per variant) is verified locally or not at all.
- **Tests gate the publish, not the merge** — the wrong end of the pipeline.

For reference, the suite is healthy today and cheap to run: 718 core tests across 52 classes (43 e2e skipped behind `-Dinclude.e2e=true`), 13 android tests per variant, all passing.

## Proposal

Add a `pr-checks.yml` modeled on the one in MediaStack-private, adapted to a Gradle/Kotlin project.

```yaml
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: pr-checks-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```

Jobs:

1. **Build & unit test** — `./gradlew build :musicmeta-core:test :musicmeta-android:test :musicmeta-okhttp:test`. Needs `actions/setup-java@v4` (temurin 17, matching the Java 17 target) and `gradle/actions/setup-gradle@v4` for the dependency cache. The Android SDK is preinstalled on `ubuntu-latest` runners.
2. **Demo build** — `cd demo && ../gradlew compileKotlin`. Cheap, and it is the canary that caught the current break.
3. **API compat** — `./gradlew apiCheck` once the binary-compatibility-validator issue lands.

Worth carrying over from the MediaStack workflow:

- **Draft-aware** — skip jobs while the PR is a draft (`github.event.pull_request.draft == false`), so a PR can be opened early for visibility at near-zero CI cost.
- **`cancel-in-progress`** — rapid pushes cost roughly one run rather than one per push.
- **E2E stays out** — the 43 e2e tests hit real third-party APIs (MusicBrainz, Deezer, Last.fm, ListenBrainz). They should stay opt-in via `-Dinclude.e2e=true` as a scheduled or on-demand job, not a PR gate, exactly as the full DinD battery is kept off the PR path in MediaStack. Rate limits and third-party flakiness must not be able to block a merge.

Once the jobs are green, add them as required status checks under Settings → Branches so they actually block merges.

`publish.yml` can then drop its own test step, or keep it as a belt-and-braces check on the tag.
comments:
Heads-up from #2 (part of #7): `apiCheck` will exist once #2 lands, so bullet 3 of the Proposal here becomes actionable rather than conditional.

Two notes for whoever picks this up:

- `binary-compatibility-validator` wires `apiCheck` into the `check` task, so `./gradlew build` already carries it. Job 1 and job 3 collapse into one command unless you want them reported as separate checks.
- #2 adds `apiCheck` to `publish.yml` as well, so the tag path is gated independently of whatever lands here. This issue remains the only thing that gates a *merge*.

The `demo/` canary job (bullet 2) stays essential — #2 fixes the two broken call sites but nothing in `./gradlew build` compiles `demo/`, so it can rot again the moment this workflow does not exist.
Landed via epic PR #11 (merge commit b8bc5ad into dev): build.yml demo-canary job compiles the demo composite build on every PR.

issues.title: Reconcile already-shipped API breaks: v0.9.2 signature, CHANGELOG backfill, 0.x semver stance
issues.body:
## Problem

The audit in #2 found several public API breaks that have **already shipped** to Maven Central and
JitPack. Adopting `binary-compatibility-validator` (#2) stops new ones; it does not decide what to do
about the ones already out there. Three linked decisions are still open, and they block narrowing the
public surface (#NEW-B placeholder) because that work needs a settled semver stance first.

## Decision 1 — the v0.9.2 `identifiers` position

Commit `4b3f08a` inserted `identifiers: EnrichmentIdentifiers? = null` into the **middle** of
`artistProfile` / `albumProfile` / `trackProfile` in `EnrichmentEngineExtensions.kt`, between `mbid`
and `types`, and shipped it in **v0.9.2 — a patch release**. Every positional argument after `mbid`
shifted one slot left.

Options:

- **Correct it** — move `identifiers` to the end of the parameter list in a v0.9.3. Restores the
  v0.9.1 positional contract, but breaks anyone who adopted v0.9.2 positionally in the meantime.
- **Leave it and document it** — add a `### Breaking Changes` entry to the v0.9.2 CHANGELOG section
  after the fact. The `.api` baseline committed in #2 records the current (shifted) shape as truth.

Whichever is chosen, `CHANGELOG.md` needs to stop describing it as backwards compatible: the v0.9.2
entry currently reads *"Backwards compatible: new parameter has a default value of `null`"*, which is
true for named callers and false for positional ones.

## Decision 2 — backfill `### Breaking Changes` in CHANGELOG

`CLAUDE.md` requires breaking changes to be documented under a `### Breaking Changes` heading. That
heading has never appeared in `CHANGELOG.md`. The #2 audit lists what is missing:

- `EnrichmentConfig.preferredArtworkSize` + `DEFAULT_ARTWORK_SIZE` deleted (312e6c8, v0.4.0) — absent
  from CHANGELOG entirely
- `EnrichmentData.IdentifierResolution` sealed variant deleted (99e3868, v0.4.0)
- `ProviderCapability.requiresIdentifier: Boolean` → `identifierRequirement: IdentifierRequirement`
  (957004a, v0.4.0) — breaks every third-party provider implementation
- `SimilarArtist.musicBrainzId` / `PopularTrack.musicBrainzId` → `identifiers: EnrichmentIdentifiers`
  (cbda960, v0.4.0) — both `@Serializable`, so persisted JSON breaks too
- Mid-list parameter insertions in v0.5.0 (`Metadata.genreTags`, also `@Serializable` so kotlinx
  element indices shifted), v0.7.0 (`EnrichmentCacheEntity`, 3 params), v0.9.0
  (`EnrichmentConfig.radioDiscoveryMode`)
- `EnrichmentEngine.enrich()` return type change and the three new interface methods without default
  bodies (b32d7d1, v0.7.0) — noted in CHANGELOG, but under `### Changed`

Decide whether to backfill historically or to draw a line at v0.9.2 and apply the rule going forward.

## Decision 3 — the 0.x semver stance

Semver arguably licenses breaking changes in 0.x. `CLAUDE.md` states the no-breaking-changes rule
with **no 0.x exception**, and the library is published to Maven Central and JitPack where consumers
exist. Either enforce the rule as written or amend `CLAUDE.md` to state the 0.x carve-out explicitly
— the current gap between stated rule and actual practice is what let the audit findings accumulate.

## Acceptance

- A recorded decision for each of the three above, in `CHANGELOG.md` and/or `CLAUDE.md`
- `CLAUDE.md`'s backwards-compatibility section says something that is actually true of this repo
- Whatever version bump the decisions imply is scheduled

Blocks the public-surface narrowing issue.
comments: Landed via epic PR #11 (merge commit b8bc5ad into dev): CHANGELOG Breaking Changes backfill, 0.x semver carve-out in CLAUDE.md, decisions recorded in STORIES.md.

issues.title: Narrow the public API surface: provider/http internals are public by omission, not design
issues.body:
## Problem

`CLAUDE.md` and `docs/agent-workflows/conventions.md` §9 both say:

> Internal code (`internal` visibility, `provider/*/` internals, `http/` infrastructure) may change freely.

In ABI terms that is **false today**. Almost nothing under `provider/` or `http/` is actually marked
`internal` — those classes are public on Maven Central and JitPack, so changing them *is* a breaking
change for any consumer who imported them.

## Evidence

Counted over `musicmeta-core/src/main/kotlin/com/landofoz/musicmeta/`, public top-level declarations
vs `internal` ones:

| Package | public | internal |
|---|---|---|
| `provider/musicbrainz/` | 15 | 2 |
| `provider/deezer/` | 12 | 0 |
| `provider/discogs/` | 11 | 0 |
| `provider/lastfm/` | 9 | 0 |
| `provider/listenbrainz/` | 9 | 0 |
| `provider/fanarttv/` | 6 | 0 |
| `provider/itunes/` | 5 | 0 |
| `provider/wikipedia/` | 5 | 0 |
| `provider/coverartarchive/` | 4 | 0 |
| `provider/lrclib/` | 4 | 0 |
| `provider/wikidata/` | 4 | 0 |
| **`provider/` total** | **84** | **2** |
| `http/` | 6 | 0 |
| `engine/` | 14 | 12 |

These are public by omission, not by design. `DiscogsMapper` and `DiscogsRelease`, for example, have
zero references anywhere outside `provider/discogs/` — they exist to serve `DiscogsProvider` and
nothing else, yet both are part of the published ABI.

Not everything listed should become `internal`. The `*Provider` classes are the intended public
surface (consumers construct them to register with the engine), as are `HttpClient`, `HttpResult`,
`HttpResponse` and `DefaultHttpClient` (a consumer supplies their own `HttpClient`). The candidates
are the `*Api`, `*Models` and `*Mapper` files behind each provider, plus the `http/` classes that are
pure infrastructure (`RateLimiter`, `CircuitBreaker`) and the `engine/` mergers and synthesizers that
are not referenced from any public signature.

## Why it matters now

#2 adopts `binary-compatibility-validator` and commits `.api` baselines that record **reality** —
including all 84 provider declarations. That was a deliberate choice: hiding them behind
`ignoredPackages` would have made the baseline lie about what ships. The consequence is that until
this issue lands, a provider-internal refactor turns `apiCheck` red and requires an `apiDump` commit.
That is honest but noisy, and it buries the one signal that matters (a real change to
`EnrichmentEngine` / `EnrichmentData`) among churn.

## Proposal

1. Classify every top-level declaration under `provider/`, `http/` and `engine/` as intended-public or
   incidentally-public. The `.api` baselines from #2 are the working inventory.
2. Mark the incidentally-public ones `internal`.
3. Run `./gradlew apiDump` — the resulting `.api` diff *is* the review artifact, and should shrink by
   roughly the counts above.
4. Document under `### Breaking Changes` in `CHANGELOG.md`. This is an ABI removal: any consumer who
   imported, say, `DeezerModels` loses it at compile time. `CLAUDE.md`'s deprecate-before-removing
   rule applies unless #4 settles on a 0.x carve-out, which is why that decision comes first.
5. Update `CLAUDE.md` / conventions.md §9 so "may change freely" is finally true.

## Acceptance

- `apiCheck` stays green through a rename inside `provider/*/` internals
- The core `.api` file describes an API surface someone actually intended
- The removal is recorded under `### Breaking Changes` with whatever version bump #4 decides

Depends on #2 (baselines exist) and #4 (semver stance settled).
comments: Landed via epic PR #11 (merge commit b8bc5ad into dev): 80 provider/http/engine internals narrowed to internal, .api baselines regenerated.

issues.title: Optional: scheduled API-drift warn job that files and auto-closes a single issue
issues.body:
## Problem

Once `binary-compatibility-validator` is wired into CI (#2, #3), an API divergence surfaces as a red
run on the PR that caused it. That is the right place for a *change* to be caught. It is the wrong
place for *drift* — a baseline that has quietly stopped matching reality for reasons other than the
PR at hand (a dependency bump changing an inherited signature, a Kotlin upgrade altering the emitted
ABI, a merge that landed a stale `.api` file).

A red run also has no memory: it goes green on the next push whether or not anyone understood why it
was red.

## Proposal

Mirror the drift-warn half of `image-drift.yml` from MediaStack-private:

- A **scheduled** job (weekly is likely enough) that checks out `dev`, runs `./gradlew apiDump`, and
  diffs the result against the committed `.api` files.
- On drift: file **one** issue, or update the existing one in place if it is already open, with the
  actual `.api` diff in the body. Never file a second issue for the same drift.
- On resolution: auto-close that issue.

The value over a red PR run is persistence and attribution — the drift gets an owner and a written
record instead of a run that scrolls away.

## Notes

- Should not duplicate the PR gate; this is about the state of `dev` over time, not about any one
  change.
- Same shape would work for the `demo/` canary (`cd demo && ../gradlew compileKotlin`), which is the
  other check that can rot silently between releases.
- Listed as explicitly optional in #2 ("Optionally mirror the drift-warn half of `image-drift.yml`").

Depends on #2 (baselines exist) and #3 (CI exists to build on).
comments: Landed via epic PR #11 (merge commit b8bc5ad into dev): scheduled api-drift.yml watch that files/auto-closes a single tracking issue on ABI drift.

issues.title: [EPIC] Public API compatibility enforcement
issues.body:
## Goal

`musicmeta` publishes three artifacts to Maven Central and JitPack, and `CLAUDE.md` states a
no-breaking-changes-without-a-major-bump contract. Nothing enforces it, and the audit in #2 shows it
has been missed repeatedly across the tag history: four mid-list parameter insertions (v0.5.0,
v0.7.0, v0.9.0, v0.9.2), four removals or renames with no deprecation cycle (v0.4.0), and
`@Deprecated` never once appearing in `musicmeta-core/src/main/`.

This epic closes the loop: make a public API change **visible** (a committed ABI baseline), make it
**gated** (CI + publish), reconcile what has already shipped, and make the codebase's actual public
surface match what the docs claim it is.

## Checklist

- [x] #2 — adopt `binary-compatibility-validator`, commit `.api` baselines for all three modules, gate
      the publish workflow, fix the positional call sites that exposed the problem
- [x] #3 — test CI on push/PR. Carries the three gate jobs: `./gradlew build` (which now includes
      `apiCheck` via `check`), the `demo/` canary compile, and `apiCheck`
- [x] #4 — reconcile already-shipped breaks: the v0.9.2 `identifiers` position, a `### Breaking
      Changes` backfill in `CHANGELOG.md`, and the 0.x semver stance in `CLAUDE.md`
- [x] #5 — narrow the public API surface: `provider/` and `http/` internals are public by omission
      (84 public vs 2 `internal` under `provider/`), which makes "may change freely" untrue today.
      Depends on #2 and #4
- [x] #6 — *optional, P3* — scheduled API-drift warn job that files and auto-closes a single issue

## Dependency order

```
#2 ─┬─> #5   (needs baselines)
    ├─> #6   (needs baselines)
    └─> #3 ──> #6
#4 ─────> #5   (needs the semver stance settled before an ABI removal)
```

#2 and #3 are independent of each other and can land in either order. #4 is a decision issue with no
code dependency and can be settled in parallel.

## Done when

- A public API change cannot reach `dev` or Maven Central without a reviewed `.api` diff
- `CLAUDE.md`'s backwards-compatibility section describes something that is actually true of the repo
- The `demo/` canary is built by CI rather than being an accidental tripwire nobody runs

Per `docs/agent-workflows/conventions.md` §4 this epic stays open as children merge into `dev`, and
closes on the release PR (`dev` → `main`).

issues.title: ci: bump GitHub Actions off deprecated Node 20 runtime
issues.body:
Both workflows pin actions whose major versions target the deprecated Node 20 runtime. CI emits this annotation on every run:

> Node.js 20 is deprecated. The following actions target Node.js 20 but are being forced to run on Node.js 24: `actions/checkout@v4`, `actions/setup-java@v4`, `gradle/actions/setup-gradle@v4`

Non-blocking today — the runner silently forces them onto Node 24 — but the compatibility shim is not permanent, and when it is withdrawn both workflows break at once. That includes `publish.yml`, which is the tag path to Maven Central, so the failure would land on a release rather than on a PR.

## Current vs latest

| Action | Pinned | Latest major |
|---|---|---|
| `actions/checkout` | `v4` | `v7` |
| `actions/setup-java` | `v4` | `v5` |
| `gradle/actions/setup-gradle` | `v4` | `v6` |

## Affected files

- `.github/workflows/build.yml` — all three actions
- `.github/workflows/publish.yml` — all three actions

## Notes

- `actions/checkout` is three majors behind; the bump should be read against each major's release notes rather than applied blind.
- `gradle/actions` v6 keeps the `gradle/actions/setup-gradle@v6` sub-action path, but its cache behaviour has changed across majors — worth confirming the build still gets cache hits after the bump.
- Verification is cheap for `build.yml` (a PR exercises it directly) but not for `publish.yml`, which only fires on a `v*` tag. Review that one by inspection, or exercise it on a throwaway tag against a snapshot target before trusting it on a real release.
comments:
Scope correction found during the #12 release review — two more affected surfaces than this issue currently lists.

**1. A third workflow file.** `#11` added `.github/workflows/api-drift.yml`, which pins the same three Node-20 actions:

- `.github/workflows/api-drift.yml:36` — `actions/checkout@v4`
- `.github/workflows/api-drift.yml:40` — `actions/setup-java@v4`
- `.github/workflows/api-drift.yml:45` — `gradle/actions/setup-gradle@v4`

**2. A fourth action, not in the table above.** `build.yml:35` pins `actions/upload-artifact@v4`, which is also on Node 20 (current major is v5). It is not listed in the Current vs latest table.

So the corrected affected-file list is:

| File | Actions |
|---|---|
| `.github/workflows/build.yml` | `checkout@v4`, `setup-java@v4`, `setup-gradle@v4`, `upload-artifact@v4` |
| `.github/workflows/publish.yml` | `checkout@v4`, `setup-java@v4`, `setup-gradle@v4` |
| `.github/workflows/api-drift.yml` | `checkout@v4`, `setup-java@v4`, `setup-gradle@v4` |

**Deliberately not folded into #12.** The release PR was reviewed for the option and it was declined, on this issue's own reasoning: `publish.yml` only fires on a `v*` tag and so cannot be exercised by a PR, and `actions/checkout` is three majors behind and needs reading against each major's release notes rather than a blind bump. Doing that inside a release PR would gate the release on unrelated research and put an unverifiable change on the Maven Central tag path. It stays a standalone PR.

Note the drift watch now shares the release path's exposure: when the Node 24 shim is withdrawn, `api-drift.yml` breaks alongside `build.yml` and `publish.yml` — so the weekly watch would go dark at the same moment the publish path does.

## Triage — re-scoped against `dev` @ d36bd85

Still real, but the inventory has grown again and two claims above need correcting. Verified against
the action manifests, the live run annotations, and the upstream deprecation notice.

### 1. A fourth workflow file, and it is SHA-pinned

`#17` (merged after the comment above was written) added `.github/workflows/provider-drift.yml`,
which carries the same three actions pinned by **commit digest** rather than by tag:

```
actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262        # v4
actions/setup-java@c1e323688fd81a25caa38c78aa6df2d33d3e20d9      # v4
gradle/actions/setup-gradle@ed408507eac070d1f99cc633dbcf757c94c7933a  # v4.4.3
```

That pinning is deliberate — the job has provider API secrets in scope, and the file says so in an
in-line comment that names this issue: *"See #10 ... it must update these digests too, not just the
tags."* A tag-only sweep silently skips this file and leaves three Node-20 actions behind. The
digest form also matters: the file notes the pin must be the **commit** SHA, not the tag-object SHA
that `refs/tags/vN` dereferences to, because that is the form pinning tooling emits and verifies.

### 2. `upload-artifact@v5` does not fix anything

The comment above says `upload-artifact`'s current major is v5. Both halves are wrong now:
`actions/upload-artifact@v5` still declares `using: 'node20'`, and the current major is v7. Bumping
that one to v5 would leave the Node-20 dependency exactly where it is.

### 3. Full inventory — 16 references, 4 files

| File | Refs | Pinning |
|---|---|---|
| `build.yml` | 7 — `checkout`, `setup-java`, `setup-gradle` in **both** the `build` and `demo-canary` jobs, plus `upload-artifact` | tag |
| `publish.yml` | 3 | tag |
| `api-drift.yml` | 3 | tag |
| `provider-drift.yml` | 3 | **commit digest** |

Minimum-safe target majors, read from each action's `action.yml`:

| Action | Pinned | First major off Node 20 | Latest major |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actions/checkout` | v4 (`node20`) | **v5** | v7 |
| `actions/setup-java` | v4 (`node20`) | **v5** | v5 |
| `gradle/actions/setup-gradle` | v4 (`node20`) | **v5** | v6 |
| `actions/upload-artifact` | v4 (`node20`) | **v6** (v5 is still `node20`) | v7 |

### 4. The urgency framing needs adjusting in both directions

The body predicts the workflows "break at once" when the shim is withdrawn. That has already been
tested in production and did not happen. Per the upstream notice, runners flipped to Node 24 by
default on **2026-06-16**; every run since then executes these actions on Node 24 already. The
v0.10.0 publish run went green on the tag path under forced Node 24 — the exact release-time failure
this issue was filed to prevent has been exercised and passed. So this is not a latent cliff.

What is real: the warning is on every run of all three exercised workflows (`build`, `demo-canary`,
`publish`, `api-drift` all carry the annotation), Node 20 is removed from the runners in the fall of
2026, and the `ACTIONS_ALLOW_USE_UNSECURE_NODE_VERSION` opt-out expires with it. A dated deadline
plus a 16-reference blast radius is more than "nice to have" — moving `priority/p3` → `priority/p2`.
Not higher: nothing is broken, and Node 24 compatibility is already empirically demonstrated.

---

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement (CI maintenance)
**Summary:** Move every GitHub Actions reference in the repository off actions whose manifests
declare the Node 20 runtime, across all four workflow files, preserving each file's existing
pinning style.

**Current behavior:**
All 16 action references resolve to majors that declare `using: node20`. The runner forces them onto
Node 24 and emits a deprecation warning on every run, including the Maven Central tag path. Runs are
green. `provider-drift.yml` pins by commit digest; the other three pin by floating major tag.

**Desired behavior:**
No action reference in `.github/workflows/**` resolves to a manifest declaring `node20`. No workflow
run emits the Node 20 deprecation annotation. `provider-drift.yml` remains digest-pinned with a
trailing version comment, and its new digests are commit SHAs rather than tag-object SHAs. The other
three files remain tag-pinned unless the maintainer decides otherwise (see below).

**Key interfaces:**
- `build.yml` — two jobs, `build` and `demo-canary`, each with its own copy of the three actions;
  plus `upload-artifact`, which is behind `if: failure()` and therefore never exercised by a green
  run. Its bump is unverified by any passing CI run and must be reasoned about by inspection.
- `publish.yml` — fires only on `v*` tags. Cannot be exercised by a PR.
- `api-drift.yml` — `workflow_dispatch` plus schedule; can be exercised on demand.
- `provider-drift.yml` — schedule plus dispatch; holds provider secrets; digest-pinned by design.
- `gradle/actions/setup-gradle` cache behavior changed across majors — confirm the build still gets
  cache hits after the bump rather than assuming it.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Every `uses:` reference across all four workflow files resolves to an action manifest
      declaring a Node runtime newer than `node20`.
- [ ] A run of `build.yml` and a run of `api-drift.yml` complete with no Node 20 deprecation
      annotation attached to any job.
- [ ] `provider-drift.yml` is still pinned by commit digest, each pin carries its version comment,
      and each digest is verifiably the action's commit SHA.
- [ ] `upload-artifact` lands on a major whose manifest is not `node20` (v5 does not satisfy this).
- [ ] Gradle cache hits are confirmed present after the `setup-gradle` bump.
- [ ] No change to what any workflow builds, tests, publishes, or writes — job graph, triggers,
      permissions, secret scope, and published artifacts are all identical before and after.

**Out of scope:**
- Any change to the publish target, signing configuration, or artifact coordinates.
- Restructuring the drift watches or the `demo-canary` job while in here.
- Adding new workflows or new gates.

**References (current at time of triage — may shift):**
- `.github/workflows/provider-drift.yml` — the in-file comment naming this issue and the digest-vs-
  tag-object-SHA distinction.
- Upstream notice: `github.blog/changelog/2025-09-19-deprecation-of-node-20-on-github-actions-runners`
  — Node 24 default from 2026-06-16, Node 20 removed from runners in the fall of 2026.

**Why this needs a human:**
Three open decisions, none of which triage can settle. First, `docs/project/workflow.md` names
`.github/workflows/**` a high-risk surface requiring explicit approval before editing and a full
independent review, at any priority — so this cannot be picked up unattended regardless of how
mechanical the diff looks. Second, the body raises how far to carry `actions/checkout`: v5 is the
minimum that clears Node 20, v7 is current, and the two intervening majors changed
`pull_request_target` checkout defaults — currency versus churn is a maintainer call, not a
lookup. Third, the body offers two verification routes for `publish.yml` (inspection only, versus a
throwaway tag against a snapshot target) and no comment has since picked one; that choice governs
how much risk the release path absorbs, and it is the reason this was kept out of #12 in the first
place. A related open question worth deciding at the same time: whether the other three files should
adopt `provider-drift.yml`'s digest pinning for consistency, or whether digest pinning stays
scoped to the secret-bearing job on purpose.

Landed via #34 (squash-merged into dev as 2002d73). Every GitHub Actions ref is off the Node 20 runtime — all four new refs independently confirmed as node24, and provider-drift's three digest pins verified against their version comments.

issues.title: ci(publish): guard that the pushed tag matches the declared build version
issues.body:
Found during the #12 release review (adversarial pass, finding #8).

`publish.yml` does no tag parsing at all. It publishes whatever `version` the three `build.gradle.kts` files declare, and derives nothing from `github.ref_name`.

## The failure

A `v0.10.0` tag pushed against build files still declaring `0.9.2` uploads GAV `io.github.famesjranko:*:0.9.2`. Maven Central is immutable and rejects the duplicate, so the outcome is:

- an immutable `v0.10.0` tag and GitHub release exist for a version that was never published
- recovery means deleting and re-pushing the tag
- the failure lands on a release, not on a PR

This is not hypothetical — it was live on `dev` during #12 and was fixed by hand-editing three files before merge. The hand-edit fixed the instance; the class of bug is untouched, and the next release can repeat it exactly.

## Suggested shape

A step before the publish step that reads the tag and asserts it matches the declared version:

```yaml
- name: Verify tag matches declared version
  shell: bash
  run: |
    set -eo pipefail
    tag_version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
    declared="$(./gradlew -q :musicmeta-core:properties | awk -F": " "/^version:/ {print \$2}")"
    if [ "$tag_version" != "$declared" ]; then
      echo "::error::tag ${GITHUB_REF_NAME} does not match declared version ${declared}"
      exit 1
    fi
```

Points to settle:

- All three modules declare `version` independently. The check should assert **all three** agree with the tag, not just core — they could drift from each other.
- Consider whether the real fix is to stop declaring the version in three places at all: a single `gradle.properties` value (or deriving from the tag) would make the inconsistency unrepresentable rather than merely detected. That is the more invasive option and wants its own decision.
- The check must run **before** the publish step so it fails while the tag is still the only artifact.

## Notes

Deliberately not folded into #12 — that PR is a release and this is a new guard needing design, not a defect in the release. Related: the release checklist added to `docs/agent-workflows/conventions.md` §8 in that PR documents the manual discipline this issue would automate.
comments:
## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement (CI guard)
**Summary:** Fail the tag-triggered publish before it uploads anything if the pushed `v*` tag does not match the version declared by all three published modules.

**Current behavior:**
The publish workflow triggers on `v*` tags and derives nothing from the tag — `github.ref_name` / `GITHUB_REF` appear nowhere in any workflow in `.github/workflows/` (verified at `6117ede` and on `origin/dev` at `d36bd85`; the file is byte-identical on both). Each of the three modules declares its own `version` literal in its own `build.gradle.kts`, and the publish step uploads whatever those literals say. Nothing reconciles the three against each other or against the tag. `apiCheck` is version-agnostic and does not help here.

The consequence is asymmetric: a tag is immutable and a Central release is immutable, but they are produced by two independent facts that nothing forces to agree. A `v0.10.0` tag over build files declaring `0.9.2` uploads GAV `…:0.9.2`, which Central rejects as a duplicate — leaving a published tag and (in current practice) a published GitHub Release for a version that never shipped, recoverable only by deleting and re-pushing the tag.

This is not theoretical. It was live on `dev` during #12 and was corrected by hand-editing three files before merge. It remained unautomated through the v0.10.0 release: PR #27 records that version consistency across the three modules was "checked by hand because `publish.yml` derives no version from the tag". The v0.10.0 publish run went green only because the human check happened to be done correctly.

PR #26 did not change this. The release checklist moved from the retired `docs/agent-workflows/conventions.md` to `docs/project/release.md`, which now states outright that "Nothing in CI derives or reconciles module versions from the tag. A mismatched tag attempts to publish the build-file version and can leave an immutable tag for an artifact that never shipped." The hazard is now documented; it is still not guarded. Documentation is the manual discipline, not the automation.

**Desired behavior:**
A tag-triggered publish run fails, with a clear error naming the tag and the offending module(s), before any artifact leaves the runner, whenever the tag version and the declared versions do not all agree. A run that passes the guard has established that tag, core, Android, and OkHttp all name the same version.

Specifics:
- The comparison is between the tag with its leading `v` stripped and the version each module actually resolves at build time — not a grep of the build files, which would miss a version set any other way.
- All three published modules are checked, not just core. They declare independently and can drift from each other as easily as from the tag; a guard that only checks core would have passed a core-only hand-edit.
- The guard runs before the publish step. A failure after upload has already produced the immutable outcome the guard exists to prevent.
- The guard must not be defeated by a silent failure in its own version lookup: an empty or unparsed declared-version must fail the run, not compare equal to nothing. The existing GPG-key step in the same workflow is the in-repo precedent for this shape (assign, assert non-empty, then use).
- A non-`v*` ref cannot reach this workflow, so no special-casing is needed for that.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] A tag whose version differs from any one of the three declared module versions fails the publish workflow at a step that runs before the Maven Central publish step, with an error message naming both the tag and the mismatching declared version.
- [ ] A tag matching all three declared versions passes the guard and the publish step still runs as it does today.
- [ ] Mismatch in the Android or OkHttp module alone — with core matching the tag — fails the run.
- [ ] The guard fails rather than passes if the declared-version lookup produces no value.
- [ ] The existing test + `apiCheck` gate on the tag path is unchanged and still runs.
- [ ] No change to any published artifact, coordinate, or public API surface — this is workflow-only.
- [ ] `docs/project/release.md` no longer asserts that nothing in CI reconciles module versions against the tag, since that would become false.

**Out of scope:**
- **Collapsing the three version declarations into one source, or deriving the version from the tag.** The issue body raises this as the stronger fix — making the inconsistency unrepresentable rather than merely detected — and explicitly defers it as "the more invasive option [that] wants its own decision". Detection here; the single-source refactor is a separate decision and should not be smuggled in alongside the guard.
- Publishing behavior, signing, or the Sonatype target.
- The test/`apiCheck` step's scope on the tag path.

**Two adjacent gaps found while verifying this, deliberately not folded in.** Both are real and both are separate from tag/version agreement; recording them here so the evidence is not lost, not to expand this issue:
1. The workflow creates no GitHub Release. That is accurate as a code fact, but it is not currently a failure: the v0.10.0 release object exists with an 8.5 KB hand-authored body, authored by the maintainer. Automating it would replace hand-written release notes with generated ones, which is a quality question, not a defect.
2. `mavenPublishing { publishToMavenCentral(SonatypeHost.CENTRAL_PORTAL) }` in all three modules sets no `automaticRelease` (vanniktech `0.30.0`), so a deployment is uploaded and validated but not released. The publish step's log shows `createStagingRepository` and `publishAllPublicationsToMavenCentralRepository` and no release task; the run reported `BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 10s`. Consequence: a green publish run does not by itself mean consumers can resolve the version. Whether that human gate is wanted is a maintainer decision, not a bug — v0.9.1 published successfully under the same configuration, so the manual step is established practice. What it does mean is that `docs/project/release.md` step 5 ("Confirm `publish.yml` succeeds and the artifacts resolve from Maven Central") is carrying the whole weight of that gate implicitly.

**References (current code at time of triage — may shift):**
- `.github/workflows/publish.yml` — trigger, and the GPG-key step whose assign-then-assert-non-empty shape is the precedent for the guard's own failure mode.
- `musicmeta-core/build.gradle.kts`, `musicmeta-android/build.gradle.kts`, `musicmeta-okhttp/build.gradle.kts` — three independent `version` literals.
- `docs/project/release.md` (on `dev`, `d36bd85`) — "Prepare on `dev`" step 2 and the paragraph documenting this exact hazard.
- PR #27 — "Version consistency" section, the hand-check this would replace.

---

**Triage note on the issue's own metadata:** `priority/p2` and `area/ci` both still hold. The v0.10.0 release completing without the guard does not lower the priority — it raises the evidence, since the manual check is now on record as the only thing standing between a mistyped version and an immutable bad tag. It does not raise it to p1 either: release cadence is low and the failure is recoverable, if noisily.

The only pre-existing comment on this issue has the body `-`, so there is no prior triage state to resume and no scope-narrowing decision recorded beyond the body itself.

**Consulted during triage:** none — the claim was verifiable directly from the workflow file, the three build files, the v0.10.0 publish run log, and the live Central metadata.

> **Correction:** an earlier comment of mine on this issue posted as a literal `-` — `gh issue comment --body -` sets the body to that string rather than reading stdin. The triage pass above correctly declined to treat the empty comment as a spec and re-verified everything independently. Restoring the intended content here as **evidence**, not as a scope change. The Agent Brief above remains the spec for this issue.

Two further gaps in the release path surfaced while executing v0.10.0. The triage pass scoped both **out** of #13, and I agree with that scoping — recording the evidence so the reasoning is on file rather than re-derived later.

## 1. `publish.yml` never creates a GitHub Release

It publishes to Maven Central and stops. No workflow creates a release object.

Observed on v0.10.0: the tag existed and `publish.yml` was green, but the Releases page still showed **v0.9.2 as Latest**, because a tag is not a Release. All eleven prior releases were created out-of-band.

**Why this is correctly out of scope for #13:** the v0.10.0 release object is hand-authored and reads better than anything a workflow would generate from a template. Automating it would *degrade* the notes. The gap is real, but the status quo is the better outcome — worth a line in the release checklist rather than automation.

## 2. The Central deployment stops in the portal, staged

All three modules declare `publishToMavenCentral(SonatypeHost.CENTRAL_PORTAL)` with no `automaticRelease` argument, and that argument appears nowhere in the repo (vanniktech 0.30.0).

Run `29842010149` logged `createStagingRepository` and `publishAllPublicationsToMavenCentralRepository`, no release task, `BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 10s`. Artifacts returned 404 from `repo1.maven.org` afterwards and the shields.io badge still read `maven-central: v0.9.2`.

**Caveat on that evidence:** the run finished only ~20 minutes before those checks, so sync latency alone could explain the 404s. The decisive evidence is historical instead — v0.9.1 published green under the identical config and *is* on Central, which means the manual Portal step is established practice, not a regression.

**Why this is correctly out of scope for #13:** it is a deliberate human gate before an immutable public artifact, not a defect. The only real problem is that it is *implicit* — nothing in `publish.yml`, `CLAUDE.md`, or the release checklist says a green publish job means the release is only half done. That is a documentation fix and a decision (keep the gate vs. set `automaticRelease = true`), not a guard to implement.

## Why they were raised here

All three — the tag/version mismatch this issue is about, plus these two — share a shape: `publish.yml` exiting green while the release is wrong or incomplete. The version guard stops a bad release from *starting*; these two stop a good one from silently *not finishing*. Only the first is a CI guard, which is why only the first belongs in this issue.
Landed via #31 (squashed into dev).

issues.title: ci(api-drift): make the tracking-issue lookup deterministic
issues.body:
Found during the #12 release review (adversarial pass, finding #13). Minor — the watch works; this hardens how it finds its own issue.

`api-drift.yml` locates its single tracking issue with:

```bash
existing="$(gh issue list --state open --limit 100 --search "${TITLE_MARKER} in:title" \
  --json number,title --jq "[.[] | select(.title | startswith(\"${TITLE_MARKER}\"))][0].number // empty")"
```

`#12` raised `--limit` from the default 30 to 100, which helps. Two gaps remain:

1. **The search is not really a prefix search.** GitHub's issue-search tokenizer strips `[` and `]`, so `[api-drift-bot] in:title` effectively searches for the words `api drift bot` in titles. The `startswith` jq filter is what actually guarantees correctness — the search is a broad prefilter. That is fine, but it means the result set can contain unrelated issues and the real tracker competes with them for the 100 slots.
2. **Results are ordered by relevance, not recency.** Past 100 matches the real tracker can still page out, and the failure mode is silent: `existing` comes back empty, the job files a *duplicate* tracker, and it does so again every week.

## Suggested fix

Filter on something the tokenizer cannot mangle. The job already applies `--label area/ci` when creating, so either:

- add a dedicated `api-drift-bot` label, applied at creation and filtered on at lookup — `gh issue list --state open --label api-drift-bot` needs no text search at all and is exact; or
- add `sort:created-asc` so ordering is deterministic and the oldest (original) tracker wins.

The label approach is preferable — it removes the text search from the correctness path entirely. Note the create call currently has a fallback for a missing label:

```bash
gh issue create --title "${TITLE}" --body-file issue-body.md --label area/ci --label enhancement || \
gh issue create --title "${TITLE}" --body-file issue-body.md
```

If the lookup depends on a label, that fallback becomes a correctness hazard — an issue created without the label is invisible to the next lookup. Create the label as part of this change and drop or rethink the fallback.

## Notes

Not folded into #12: that PR is a release, and this is a hardening change to a workflow that has not yet run a single scheduled cycle. Worth doing before the first Monday it fires.
comments:
## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement (CI hardening)
**Summary:** Retrofit the label-first tracking-issue lookup — already shipped in the provider drift watch — onto the API drift watch, so the watch finds its own tracker without depending on a text search.

**Verified still present.** The lookup in the API drift watch is unchanged since the watch was added; the fixes that landed around v0.10.0 (`c056dda` pipefail masking, `774f314` body budgets, `bb38739` the `|| true` guard on this very call) raised `--limit` to 100 and stopped the call aborting the step, but none of them changed the *mechanism*. The correctness path is still `--search "<marker> in:title"` plus a `startswith` jq filter. Identical on `main` and `dev`.

**Current behavior:**
The watch resolves its tracker with a title search. GitHub's issue-search tokenizer strips bracket punctuation, so the marker degrades to three ordinary words ranked by relevance. The `startswith` filter prevents false *positives* — it cannot prevent a false *negative*. Once enough open issues match those tokens, the real tracker can rank out of the 100-result window, the lookup returns empty, and the run routes to `create`. That is silent, and it repeats every Monday.

**Desired behavior:**
The lookup keys on a dedicated bot-only label, exactly as the provider drift watch does: label lookup first; title search only as a fallback for the case where the label was removed during triage, and when that fallback hits, re-apply the label with a `::warning::`; create with the label, with a label-less `create` as last resort so a deleted label cannot stop the watch filing anything at all. That three-layer shape is not decoration — the provider watch needed all three because `gh issue list --label` on a *deleted* label exits 0 with empty output, which would otherwise route every run to `create`.

**Scope is this one workflow.** The sibling provider drift watch does **not** share the defect — it shipped with the label-first lookup and its inline comment already names this issue as the retrofit follow-up. Nothing here should touch it.

**Key interfaces:**
- Tracking-issue lookup contract — resolution must not depend on issue-search text ranking.
- A new repository label, bot-only, named to match the existing sibling label convention. Creating it is a prerequisite of the change; if it is absent the workflow must degrade to the title fallback rather than fail.
- Issue creation — the label must be applied at create time, or the next lookup cannot see the issue.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Tracker resolution succeeds regardless of how many open issues match the title marker's tokens.
- [ ] A tracker whose label was manually removed is still found, and the label is re-applied automatically.
- [ ] A missing or deleted label never prevents the watch from filing an issue.
- [ ] Newly created trackers carry the label, so the following run's lookup finds them.
- [ ] The healthy path still auto-closes exactly one tracker and never closes an unrelated issue.
- [ ] Every `run:` block still passes `bash -n`; no change to triggers, permissions, or the `concurrency` no-cancel guarantee.

**One hazard to design against, in both watches:**
The label lookup takes `.[0]` from a list ordered newest-first, so **any** open issue carrying the bot label becomes a candidate tracker. If a human-filed issue ever carries it and is newer than the real tracker, the watch will retitle, overwrite, or auto-close that human issue. The label must be reserved strictly for bot-filed trackers — worth a line in the label description and, if cheap, an ownership check before the destructive `edit`/`close` calls.

**Out of scope:**
- The provider drift watch (already fixed).
- The `sort:created-asc` alternative floated in the body — superseded by the label approach, which the sibling watch has already shipped and adversarially reviewed.
- Any change to the drift-detection logic, the diff/log byte budgets, or the demo canary arm.
- The Node-20 runtime bump (#10) and the action digest pins.

**Why `priority/p3` is right:** the failure needs >100 open issues matching the marker's tokens. At this repo's scale that is remote. issues.title: ci: scheduled provider-API drift watch — a provider change silently breaks released versions
issues.body:
Found while proving out the ABI drift watch (#6 / #12). **This is the inverse gap, and it is the more dangerous one.**

## The two drifts are not the same thing

| | Watches | Protects | Covered? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `apiCheck` + `api-drift.yml` | musicmeta's own published Kotlin ABI | *our consumers* from *us* | ✅ shipped in v0.10.0, proven end-to-end |
| **this issue** | third-party provider JSON/endpoints | *musicmeta* from *them* | ❌ **nothing** |

Grep the committed baselines for any provider response field — `recording_name`, `release_name`, `artist-credit` — and you get **0 hits**. The `.api` files describe our signatures. They cannot see MusicBrainz's wire format, and were never meant to.

## Why this is worse than "no coverage"

**1. The failure is silent by construction.** Every parser uses `org.json`'s `opt*` family:

```kotlin
title      = item.optString("recording_name", ""),
albumName  = item.optString("release_name")?.takeIf { it.isNotBlank() },
```

`optString` returns the default on a missing key — it does not throw. A renamed field yields `""`, which flows through as a **successful** enrichment containing nothing. No exception, no `NotFound`, no failed build.

**2. It has already happened, and shipped.** From `CHANGELOG.md` v0.9.1:

> **Empty top track titles from ListenBrainz** — API parser read `track_name` but the API returns `recording_name`, causing all TopTrack titles to be empty strings
> **Missing album names from ListenBrainz top tracks** — parser looked for a nested `release` object but the API returns `release_name` as a top-level field

Two field renames, both shipped to users, both found by observation rather than by a test.

**3. Bad data persists past the fix.** That same release carries a migration note telling users to clear their cache, because the empty values were written through `EnrichmentCache` with their TTLs (up to 7 days). The blast radius outlives the patch.

**4. Nothing runs the tests that would catch it.** `grep -rn "e2e" .github/workflows/` returns nothing.

## The part that makes this P1

**A provider can break a released version with zero commits to this repo.** Every other gate here is change-triggered: a PR, a push, a tag. This failure arrives from outside, on someone else's deploy schedule, while our tree is untouched and every check is green. The response is a patch release (`0.10.1` — permitted, it is a bugfix, not an API break), and today the clock on that starts when a **user** reports it.

That is the whole argument for a *scheduled* watch: the trigger is external, so the detector must be too.

## What already exists, and is better than expected

The e2e suite is genuinely fit for this. Assertions are content-level, not liveness-level:

```kotlin
assertTrue("Bio should be substantial", bio.text.length > 50)
assertTrue("Confidence >= 0.80", success.confidence >= 0.80f)
assertEquals("Should use provided MBID", "a74b1b7f-71a5-4011-9441-d0b5e4122711", success.resolvedIdentifiers?.musicBrainzId)
assertNotNull("Should have genres or label", data.genres ?: data.label)
```

`bio.text.length > 50` catches exactly the v0.9.1 empty-string failure. This suite would have caught it.

**Correction to a number we quote a lot:** the suite is **70 tests across 5 classes**, not 43. The 43 figure is what the build reports as skipped, and it is precisely the three classes gated in `@Before` (13 + 13 + 17). The other two gate in `@BeforeClass` (`EdgeAnalysisTest` 11, `V060EdgeTest` 16), which skips at class level and is not counted per-test. Worth normalising on one gating style so the count means something.

## Proposed design — reuse the pattern proven in #12

`.github/workflows/provider-drift.yml`, deliberately near-identical to `api-drift.yml`, whose file/update/auto-close cycle was verified end-to-end (clean → drift → restore) before this issue was written:

- **Schedule** — daily or weekly. Provider deploys are external; pick the cadence against how fast we would want to know.
- **Runs** `./gradlew :musicmeta-core:test -Dinclude.e2e=true`.
- **Files / updates / auto-closes a single `[provider-drift-bot]` tracking issue**, with the failing test names and assertion messages in the body. Use a dedicated **label** for the lookup rather than a title search — see #14 for why the text-search form is not deterministic.
- **Never gating.** `conventions.md` §6 is right that third-party rate limits and outages must not block a merge. This does not change that — it gives the signal an owner instead of no home at all.
- **`continue-on-error` + `shell: bash`** on the Gradle step. Both are load-bearing: without `shell: bash` a `gradlew | tee` pipeline reports tee's exit status and the failure is masked. That exact bug shipped in `api-drift.yml` and was caught in review — do not re-introduce it.
- **Byte-cap every variable-length body section.** GitHub caps issue bodies at 65536 characters.

### Open questions

1. **Secrets.** E2E needs `ApiKeyConfig` values — Last.fm, Fanart.tv, Discogs, ListenBrainz token. These are not currently repo secrets. Which providers can be exercised keyless (MusicBrainz, Deezer, iTunes, LrcLib, Wikidata, Wikipedia, CoverArtArchive) versus needing a secret? A keyless-only first cut would cover most providers with no secret-management work.
2. **Flake versus drift.** A 503 is noise; a renamed field is signal. Both surface as a red test. Consider re-running failures once and only filing on a repeat, or splitting "provider unreachable" from "provider returned unexpected shape" in the assertions.
3. **Pinned fixtures.** The strongest form is asserting on a *stable* entity (the AC/DC and Radiohead MBIDs already used) so a content change upstream is distinguishable from a schema change.
4. **Should it also watch the released artifact?** The scheduled job tests `dev`. The user-facing risk is the *published* version. Since they are the same code between releases, testing `dev` is a good proxy — but worth stating explicitly rather than assuming.

## Response playbook once it fires

A confirmed provider break means a patch release: fix the parser, add a unit test with the new shape pinned as a fixture, ship `0.10.x`. The 0.x carve-out permits it — a parser fix keeps the public signature and ABI stable, so it is a patch, not a minor.

Related: #13 (tag/version guard), #14 (deterministic tracker lookup — apply the same fix here from the start).
comments:
Landed in #17, squash-merged to `dev` as ca51fb3.

Closed manually per the workflow contract §4 — `dev` is not the default branch, so `closes #16` does not fire on a child merge.

**What shipped:** `.github/workflows/provider-drift.yml` — daily scheduled run of the 70-test e2e suite against live provider APIs, filing/updating/auto-closing a single `[provider-drift-bot]` tracker. Never gating.

**On the open questions in this issue:**
1. *Secrets* — all four (`LASTFM_API_KEY`, `FANARTTV_API_KEY`, `DISCOGS_TOKEN`, `LISTENBRAINZ_TOKEN`) are configured as repo secrets, so the watch covers all 11 providers rather than a keyless-only first cut. A missing key is reported as misconfiguration, not drift.
2. *Flake vs drift* — the suite is retried once after a 60s pause before anything is filed.
3. *Pinned fixtures* — unchanged; the suite's existing stable-entity assertions are used as-is.
4. *Released artifact vs `dev`* — the job checks out `dev` explicitly, and this is now stated in the workflow rather than assumed.

**Not yet exercised.** GitHub registers `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch` only from the default branch, so the watch stays inert until a release carries it to `main` — the same path `api-drift.yml` took. All verification to date is local harness against the extracted `run:` blocks plus live API measurement.

Follow-ups tracked separately: three unreachable-state nits in the summary path (unguarded `head -1`, `wc -l` undercount on a missing final newline, zero-length fence), and #14/#10 as already noted.

issues.title: docs: add a comment-style rule to CLAUDE.md and the contract
issues.body:
## Problem

Neither `CLAUDE.md`'s **Code Style** section nor §9 of the workflow contract says anything about comments. In practice this has produced comments that restate the code beneath them, narrate the history of how a line came to exist, and outlive the code they described.

`.github/workflows/provider-drift.yml` is the clearest example: roughly 40% of the file is comment, much of it recounting which review round changed what and why a previous approach was replaced. That history belongs in the PR and the commit message, not in the file, where it cannot be verified and goes stale silently.

## Rule

Add to `CLAUDE.md` **Code Style**:

> **Comments:** Explain only non-obvious constraints, traps, guards, or safety rationale. Do not restate code or preserve history; put that in issues, PRs, or docs. Remove comments when the related code is removed.

## Why also in the contract

§9 of `docs/agent-workflows/conventions.md` restates `CLAUDE.md`'s code-style rules and is the surface the adversarial reviewer subagent actually checks against. Adding the rule to `CLAUDE.md` alone would leave it unenforced, and would add one more instance of the §9-vs-`CLAUDE.md` drift already tracked separately. Both files get it, with `CLAUDE.md` remaining authoritative.

## Scope

Docs only — `CLAUDE.md` +1 line, `conventions.md` +4. No code, no CI change. Always-checks only per §6's docs-only row.
comments:
Landed in #20, squash-merged to `dev`.

Closed manually per contract §4 — `dev` is not the default branch.

**Scope changed during review.** The rule is stated in `CLAUDE.md` only. The original version also mirrored it into §9 of the contract; that hunk was dropped after a design review found §9 to be 100% restatement of `CLAUDE.md` and the root of this repo's recurring documentation drift. Routing §9 rather than copying into it is #21.

**Adversarial review caught a real contradiction**: the rule as first drafted was an exhaustive whitelist, while **Testing Patterns** mandates Given-When-Then narration and forbids bare section markers. Measured 1,450 descriptive Given/When/Then lines in the tree that one rule would compel and the other forbid. The carve-out is scoped by comment *form* rather than file location, which covers those 1,450 without also rescuing the 541 bare markers — those now fail both rules in the same direction.

Does not retrofit existing comments; a grep of main-source Kotlin for history narration returns zero hits, so the retrofit surface is small.

issues.title: docs: route §9 of the workflow contract to CLAUDE.md instead of restating it
issues.body:
## Problem

§9 of `docs/agent-workflows/conventions.md` is a restatement of `CLAUDE.md`. Its own preamble admits it — *"Sourced from `CLAUDE.md` — that file remains authoritative"* — and a copy with an authoritative source has no re-sync trigger. The canonical doc gets edited, the copy does not, and the reviewer subagent then enforces the stale half against a diff the canonical doc permits.

**Measured:** §9 is 38 non-blank lines, all six blocks mapping 1:1 onto a `CLAUDE.md` heading. Contract-local rules: zero.

## It has already rotted, four ways

1. **Stale, and wrong in the expensive direction.** §9 still says *"No breaking changes to public API without a major version bump."* The 0.x carve-out that repudiated this landed in `12ba7ac`, which touched `CHANGELOG.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `STORIES.md` — not this file. A reviewer applying §9 blocks every sanctioned `0.x.0` break and tells the author to bump the major version, which is unactionable pre-1.0.
2. **Missing the ABI caveat.** §9's append-at-the-end rule has no trace of `CLAUDE.md`'s *"appending is the source-compatible floor, not a full ABI guarantee"*. Verified by runtime reproduction: appending a parameter **with a default at the end** still changes the JVM descriptor, and a pre-compiled consumer gets `NoSuchMethodError` — including for `data class` `copy`/`componentN` and the synthetic `$default` bridge.
3. **Lossy in four of six blocks.** Modeling drops the collection-wrapper rule; Testing drops Robolectric and the `-Dinclude.e2e=true` gate; Conventions drops the package and group ID; Code style drops "no magic".
4. **The `demo/` canary claim it copies exists in six files** — `CLAUDE.md`, this file twice (§6 and §9), `STORIES.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `build.yml` — and `git log` shows three consecutive commits (`774f314`, `64c85bc`, `bb38739`) doing nothing but re-correcting it across them. It is *still* wrong in some copies.

## The copy buys nothing

`ship-issue` and `ship-pr` both begin by reading `CLAUDE.md` to find this contract. It is already open on every run. §9 saves zero reads; it only supplies a second, staler answer.

**The decisive evidence is inside this file.** §8 already handles the same versioning rule *by pointer*: *"Choose the number against the 0.x carve-out in `CLAUDE.md`."* That pointer is still correct today. §9's copy of the same rule is wrong. Same file, same author, same day — the pointer survived and the copy rotted.

## Proposed change

Replace §9's body with a route naming the canonical sections the reviewer must open and read at review time, keeping inline **only** invariants that have no home in a canonical doc.

Any assertion that turns out to be unique to §9 rather than a copy gets migrated into `CLAUDE.md` rather than deleted — a content-preservation diff runs first, and nothing is dropped silently.

## Companion change (already made, outside this repo)

The global `ship-init` skill instructed the contract author to *"pull these from `CLAUDE.md` where they already exist"* — the instruction that manufactures the copy. It now says route, do not restate. `ship-issue` / `ship-pr` now tell the reviewer to open the canonical documents §9 routes to, which is what makes a thin §9 safe.

## Not in scope

The same routing treatment is owed to §6's canary row, §5's `apiCheck`/`apiDump` paragraph, and §8's doc-trigger rows that restate `CLAUDE.md`'s Documentation table. Follow-up.
comments:
Landed in #24, squash-merged to `dev`. Closed manually per §4 — `dev` is not the default branch.

**What shipped**, beyond the §9 deletion:

- **Retitled** `Workflow Contract` → `Shipping Conventions`. The old title, plus a subtitle calling the file "the project-specific half of the ship-issue and ship-pr procedures", is what licensed §3 and §7 to be written as commentary on those skills' command-line flags. The boundary is now stated in the file: *`CLAUDE.md` says what project documentation applies and what the code-level rules are; this file says how work gets from an issue to a published release.*
- **Dead tooling references removed.** §3's two flags and §7's framing as "where those flags are rejected" — vacuous once the flags were gone.
- **One deliberate tightening**, called out rather than smuggled in: those bullets used to constrain an opt-in flag sitting above an already-autonomous baseline, so P2 work could run unattended. They now constrain behaviour, so P2 and above get a human in the loop.
- **One migration that mattered:** §9's no-attribution rule covered *"any commit, PR, issue comment, or anything else that leaves this machine"*, while `CLAUDE.md` said only *"commits or PR messages"*. Deleting §9 without widening `CLAUDE.md` would have narrowed the rule to whatever a contributor happened to have in their own user-level config.

**Preservation:** independently re-derived twice — 41 atomic assertions, zero homeless, every absence grep-proven rather than asserted.

Three rounds of adversarial review caught three false claims I had written into the governance text, including "enforced it for months" (actual: 2h23m) and an assertion count that did not sum. Worth recording, since the PR's own thesis is that false claims in governance text are defects.
