issues.title: core: README claims enrich() never throws, but the cache read is outside the try block
issues.body:
## Problem

`README.md` ("Partial failure resilience") states:

> The engine never throws from `enrich()` — all failures are represented as typed results.

That appears to be false. In `musicmeta-core/src/main/kotlin/com/landofoz/musicmeta/engine/DefaultEnrichmentEngine.kt`, the cache read calling `cache.get(entityKeyFor(request, type), type)` sits **outside** the `try` block, and that block's only handler is `catch (_: TimeoutCancellationException)`. An exception thrown by an `EnrichmentCache` implementation therefore propagates out of `enrich()` uncaught.

`RoomEnrichmentCache` performs disk I/O, so this is not a theoretical implementation — though whether Room throws under realistic conditions for this DAO is **unverified**, and confirming that is part of the work.

## Why it matters

The claim is load-bearing: it is the reason a consumer would call `enrich()` without a try/catch. If a cache failure can escape, every consumer following the README is missing a handler.

## Decide, then make code and doc agree

- **Guard it** — wrap the cache read so a cache failure degrades to a fresh fetch (treat as uncached) and keep the README claim; or
- **Narrow the claim** — say the engine never throws on *provider* failure, and document that a throwing cache propagates.

The first is probably right: a cache is an optimisation, and a broken one should not take down enrichment.

## Verification

`./gradlew :musicmeta-core:test`, plus a new test using a `FakeEnrichmentCache` whose `get` throws — asserting the chosen behaviour either way.

Found by applying the "claims about behaviour must be executed, not asserted" idea to an existing doc.
comments:
Fixed in #25, squashed onto `dev` as 41a4460.

Guarded rather than narrowing the claim, per the issue's own recommendation — a cache is an optimisation and a broken one shouldn't take enrichment down.

Scope was wider than the report: five call sites on the `enrich()` path, not one. The `forceRefresh` invalidation, the read, the `STALE_IF_ERROR` stale read, and both `put` calls all sat outside the try. Guarding only the read would have left the README claim false.

Verified with the confirmation you asked for: a `FakeEnrichmentCache` with per-operation and per-key throw injection, and each test checked against the bug — reverting the fix makes all four engine-level tests fail, so they aren't no-ops. 786 tests / 0 failures, `apiCheck` green, public API unchanged.

Two adjacent defects of the same class surfaced and are deliberately **not** fixed here:
- `ResultMerger.merge` and `CompositeSynthesizer.synthesize` are public consumer extension points called with no try/catch, so a throwing implementation still escapes `enrich()`. Documented in the README for now.
- `resolveIdentity` catches bare `Exception` inside the `withTimeout` block, so it swallows `TimeoutCancellationException` and masks the deadline until the next suspension point.

Both want their own issues.

issues.title: docs: one fact, several homes — finish deduplicating the canary claim and the contract
issues.body:
## Problem

The claim about what the `demo/` canary proves regarding mid-list parameter insertion is stated in **six** places, and `git log` shows three consecutive commits (`774f314`, `64c85bc`, `bb38739`) doing nothing but re-correcting it across them. Some copies are **still wrong**.

The correct rule, verified against Kotlin 2.1.0 in both directions:

> A mid-list insertion carrying a default stays invisible to the compiler **only** when the rebound arguments still type-check **and** every parameter from the insertion point onward already has a default. Either condition failing breaks the build — a type error, or `no value passed for parameter` once the shifted arguments run out before a required one.

Reproduced:

```
// v1: fun profile(name: String, note: String)
// v2: fun profile(name: String, label: String = "def", note: String)
// caller (unchanged): profile("hello", "world")
e: Main.kt:2:39 No value passed for parameter 'note'.      // all String — no type clash possible
```

With every trailing parameter defaulted, the same shape compiles silently. `albumProfile` was that shape, which is why v0.9.2 could only ever have been caught by the type check — and by luck it was, `Set<EnrichmentType>` not binding to `EnrichmentIdentifiers?`.

## Sites still carrying the refuted or mis-attributed version

- `docs/agent-workflows/conventions.md` §6 — *"fails to compile only if it also produces a type error"*
- `.github/workflows/build.yml` — same, **plus** the mis-attribution *"(An inserted parameter with no default does fail outright, but that form is banned anyway.)"* — that error mode also arises from a **defaulted** insertion
- `STORIES.md`
- `CHANGELOG.md` and `ROADMAP.md` reference it in passing

`CLAUDE.md` has been corrected.

## Remedy

Correct the wrong copies, then **reduce the number of copies**. The response to a claim that has needed three rounds of synchronised correction is to have one home for it and route to that home, not to re-sync six files a fourth time. `CLAUDE.md` is the natural home; everything else should point at it. See #21, which does this for §9.



---

## Scope extended: finish the deduplication

#24 retired §9, which was pure restatement of `CLAUDE.md`. Three duplicated regions remain, and they are the same defect as the canary claim above — one fact, several homes, no re-sync trigger.

The boundary to apply:

> `CLAUDE.md` tells an agent **what project documentation applies** and what the code-level rules are.
> `docs/agent-workflows/conventions.md` tells it **how this repository ships work**.

**1. §8's doc-update trigger table → point at `CLAUDE.md`'s Documentation table.** The rows for `STORIES.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` and `ROADMAP.md` restate what `CLAUDE.md` already says about which doc is for what. Keep only the triggers that are genuinely shipping-specific — the release row, the breaking-change row — and route the rest.

**2. §5's `apiCheck`/`apiDump` paragraph → route.** It *explains what the check does* ("a failure there is not a flaky check — it means the public API changed"). That is check semantics, which belongs with the build documentation. §5 should say *when to run it*, not *what it means*.

**3. §6 keeps the mapping, loses the explanations.** The changed-area → verification table is the highest-value content in the file and should stay authoritative. But individual cells that explain what a check proves — notably the public-API row's canary essay, which is the copy this issue is about — should route to `CLAUDE.md` instead of restating.

**Sizing check.** After this, the file lands around 110–120 lines. That stays comfortably above the ~20–40 line threshold at which folding it into `CLAUDE.md` entirely would be the better call, so it remains a separate routed doc. The release checklist alone is ~25 lines of knowledge that exists nowhere else and that CI actively cannot enforce — `publish.yml` derives no version from the tag.

**Verification:** docs-only, so always-checks only per §6. Plus a grep afterwards proving no claim about check semantics survives in two places.
comments:
## Triage — re-scoped in place

Verified against `origin/dev` @ `d36bd85` (post-#26, post-v0.10.0). Two findings change what this issue is.

### 1. The premise "`CLAUDE.md` has been corrected" is false

`CLAUDE.md`'s canary blockquote is **byte-identical between `main` and `dev`** (`git diff origin/main:CLAUDE.md origin/dev:CLAUDE.md` shows only the two Documentation-table rows swapped by #26). It still carries both defects this issue reports elsewhere — the refuted claim *and* the mis-attribution:

> the break then surfaces only if the rebinding also produces a **type** error. (An inserted parameter with *no* default fails outright with "no value passed for parameter" — but that form is already forbidden outright below.)

That is the same sentence pair as `.github/workflows/build.yml`. So the routing plan ("`CLAUDE.md` is the natural home; everything else should point at it") cannot be executed as written: **the home is one of the wrong copies.** Correcting it is a precondition, not a completed step.

### 2. The corrected rule is confirmed, and it is the artifact worth keeping

Independently reproduced against **Kotlin 2.1.0** (`kotlin-compiler-embeddable-2.1.0`), both directions:

```
// fun profile(name: String, label: String = "def", note: String)
// caller: profile("hello", "world")
error: no value passed for parameter 'note'.     // all String — no type clash available
```

```
// fun profile(name: String, label: String = "def", note: String = "n")
// caller: profile("hello", "world")             // compiles clean, silently rebound
```

The rule as stated in the body holds. A defaulted mid-list insertion is invisible **only** when the rebound arguments still type-check **and** the trailing parameters left unbound all have defaults. `"no value passed for parameter"` is not exclusive to undefaulted insertions — that is the mis-attribution.

### 3. Site list, re-verified against dev

| Site | State |
|---|---|
| `CLAUDE.md` (canary blockquote) | **still wrong** — refuted claim + mis-attribution |
| `.github/workflows/build.yml` (`demo-canary` comment) | **still wrong** — same two defects |
| `STORIES.md` (2026-07-21 canary entry) | **still wrong** — "breaks compilation only when the rebinding also produces a type error" |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | **not a carrier.** It says the canary no longer detects a mid-list insertion and `apiCheck` is the position guard. That is accurate; leave it. |
| `ROADMAP.md` | **not a carrier.** It mentions the canary and the four mid-list insertions but asserts nothing about check semantics. Leave it. |
| `docs/agent-workflows/conventions.md` §6 | **moot** — file deleted by #26 |

### 4. The "Scope extended" half is largely delivered or moot

#26 replaced `conventions.md` with `docs/project/workflow.md` + `docs/project/release.md`. Against that:

- **Item 2 (§5 `apiCheck`/`apiDump` semantics → route):** done. `workflow.md` → *Verification* states when to run, and the public-API row routes with "review the API diff against `CLAUDE.md` → **Backwards Compatibility**". No check-semantics essay survives.
- **Item 3 (§6 keeps the mapping, loses the explanations):** done. The changed-surface → evidence table survived intact; the canary essay did not.
- **Item 1 (§8 doc-trigger table → point at `CLAUDE.md`):** superseded, and **out of scope here.** `workflow.md` → *Commit and documentation routing* is a change-trigger table; `CLAUDE.md`'s Documentation table is a what-each-doc-is-for table. Post-#26 those are different axes, not one fact in two homes.
- **The sizing check (110–120 lines) is moot** — the file it sized no longer exists.

What survives is the first half only: one false claim, three live copies.

## Agent Brief

**Category:** documentation (correction of a verifiably false claim)
**Summary:** Replace the refuted mid-list-rebinding explanation with the Kotlin-2.1.0-verified rule in the three places that still carry it, and make `CLAUDE.md` the single authority the other two route to.

**Current behavior:**
`CLAUDE.md`, `build.yml` and `STORIES.md` each assert that a defaulted mid-list parameter insertion breaks compilation *only* when the rebinding also produces a type error, and attribute the `"no value passed for parameter"` failure mode exclusively to undefaulted insertions. Both halves are false. The surrounding *conclusion* — a green canary proves consumers compile, not that argument order is unchanged; `apiCheck` is the position guard — is correct and must survive unchanged.

**Desired behavior:**
One authoritative statement of the rule in `CLAUDE.md`. `build.yml`'s `demo-canary` comment and the `STORIES.md` entry stop restating the mechanism and point at it. The two non-carriers (`CHANGELOG.md`, `ROADMAP.md`) are not touched.

**Key surfaces:**
- `CLAUDE.md` canary blockquote — owns the rule. Both conditions stated (type-check survival *and* trailing defaults), with the `"no value passed"` mode correctly attributed to defaulted insertions too.
- `.github/workflows/build.yml` `demo-canary` comment — keep the "why this job exists" and "not a required check" content; drop the mechanism sentences in favour of the existing `see CLAUDE.md` pointer.

issues.title: core: a throwing ResultMerger or CompositeSynthesizer escapes enrich()
issues.body:
Follow-up from #22, which fixed the same defect class on the cache path.

> **Note:** this issue was filed with an empty body due to a tooling error on my part (`gh issue create --body -` sets the body to a literal `-`; only `--body-file -` reads stdin). Restored here, with corrections from the triage pass folded in.

## Problem

`ResultMerger` and `CompositeSynthesizer` are public, consumer-implementable extension points, registered via `EnrichmentEngine.Builder.addMerger` / `addSynthesizer`. `resolveTypes` in `DefaultEnrichmentEngine` calls both with no `try`/`catch`:

- `mergers[mergeType]?.merge(filtered)`
- `synthesizers[compositeType]?.synthesize(resolved, identityResult, request)`

`enrich()`'s only handler is `catch (_: TimeoutCancellationException)`, so an exception from a consumer's implementation propagates out of `enrich()`.

Confirmed by probe against `dev` with a merger whose `merge` throws:

```
THREW IllegalStateException: merger boom
```

## Collateral loss — corrected

An earlier draft of this issue claimed the failure "cancels every other type resolving concurrently". That is imprecise, and the triage pass corrected it:

- Regular types are fully `awaitAll()`-ed **before** the mergeable `async`es launch, so they are **not** cancelled — they are computed and then discarded when the exception unwinds.
- Only the concurrent *merge* coroutines are genuinely cancelled.
- Synthesis runs sequentially after both awaits, so a throwing **synthesizer** cancels nothing.
- Cache hits collected before the fan-out are discarded too.

So the loss is real — the entire call's results are thrown away, including work that already succeeded and cached data that cost nothing — but the mechanism is "discarded", not "cancelled", except for sibling merges.

## Shipped strategies are unaffected

Verified across all eight built-ins wired by the Builder (six mergers, two synthesizers), not just the two named originally:

- Every merger opens with an `isEmpty()` guard that keeps `maxOf` / `first()` off an empty list.
- `GenreAffinityMatcher` guards empty candidates.
- `TimelineSynthesizer`'s `parts[0]` is safe because `split` always yields at least one element.

So this is reachable only by a consumer implementing the interfaces themselves.

## The design question, and the precedent that settles it

The obvious counter-argument is that a consumer's own callback exception *should* surface loudly rather than be swallowed. That fails against this project's established stance:

`EnrichmentProvider` is also public and consumer-registrable via `addProvider`, and a throwing provider **is** caught — at both `ProviderChain` call sites — and converted to `EnrichmentResult.Error(type, provider.id, message, e)`. `EnrichmentCache` received the same treatment in #22.

That leaves mergers and synthesizers as the one unguarded extension point out of three. The inconsistency is the argument, not the "never throws" promise on its own.

The precedent also settles the shape of the fix: **report as a typed `Error`, do not silently degrade.** The cache's degrade-to-miss behaviour does not transfer — a merger produces the type's result, so swallowing the failure would be indistinguishable from a genuine `NotFound`.

## On the README

`README.md` currently documents the present behaviour as intended:

> The guarantee covers provider and cache failures. It does not extend to code *you* supply through other extension points.

That paragraph was written during #22 under scope discipline, as a known-limitation note — alongside the still-standing headline "The engine never throws from `enrich()`" and ROADMAP's "Resilient by default". It records a deferral, not a rejection. Fixing this means deleting it.

## Scope

The fix is `internal`-only; `apiCheck` stays green and no public signature changes.

## Verification

`./gradlew :musicmeta-core:test`, plus tests using a throwing `ResultMerger` and a throwing `CompositeSynthesizer` asserting the chosen behaviour, and one asserting that an unrelated type still resolves in the same `enrich()` call.

## Not a defect: the `resolveIdentity` catch

While investigating, `resolveIdentity`'s bare `catch (e: Exception)` — which sits inside the `withTimeout` block — was suspected of swallowing `TimeoutCancellationException` and masking the enrichment deadline. **It does not.** Probed with a 100ms timeout against a 5s identity provider:

```
RETURNED Error kind=TIMEOUT
```

Cancellation is re-asserted at the next suspension point, so the deadline still produces the correct typed result. The only residue is that the warning logs "Identity resolution failed" rather than naming the timeout. Recorded here so the same false suspicion is not re-derived.
comments:
## Agent Brief

> **Note on the issue body:** this issue was filed with an empty body (a bare `-`), so the title was the whole claim. It has been verified independently against `dev` and this brief now carries the substance.

**Category:** enhancement (defensive hardening) — reclassified from `bug`, reasoning below
**Summary:** `ResultMerger` and `CompositeSynthesizer` are the only consumer-supplied extension points whose exceptions still escape `enrich()`. Guard them the way providers and the cache already are: convert to a typed `Error` scoped to the type that failed.

**The claim is real.** Inside the engine's type fan-out, the merge step and the composite-synthesis step both invoke the consumer-supplied strategy with no `try`. The only handler wrapping that whole region catches `TimeoutCancellationException`, so anything else propagates out of `enrich()` unconverted.

**Blast radius — larger than "that one type fails".** The fan-out runs inside a `coroutineScope`, so the throw aborts the scope and `enrich()` returns nothing at all:
- Results for every *other* requested type are lost. Regular types are already awaited by the time mergers run, so they are computed and then discarded rather than cancelled — the practical outcome is the same.
- Concurrently-running sibling *merge* coroutines are genuinely cancelled mid-flight.
- Cache hits collected before the fan-out are lost too. Ten requested types, nine served from cache, one custom merger throwing → the caller gets an exception instead of the nine.

A synthesizer throw is the same loss, minus the sibling cancellation — synthesis runs sequentially after the awaits, so nothing is in flight.

**Shipped strategies are not affected — verified for all of them, not just the two named.** The Builder wires six mergers (`GenreMerger`, `SimilarArtistMerger`, `SimilarTrackMerger`, two `ArtworkMerger` instances, `TopTrackMerger`) and two synthesizers (`TimelineSynthesizer`, `GenreAffinityMatcher`). Every merger opens with an `isEmpty()` guard, which is precisely what keeps the later `maxOf { }` / `first()` off an empty list. `GenreAffinityMatcher` guards its empty-candidates case; `TimelineSynthesizer` guards non-artist requests and its `split("-")` indexing is safe because `split` always yields at least one element. No `!!` anywhere (CLAUDE.md forbids it). So this is not an observable defect in stock configuration — it is reachable only through `addMerger` / `addSynthesizer`.

**Why this is not `wontfix`.** The obvious counter-argument is that a consumer's own callback throwing is the consumer's bug and should propagate loudly. That argument does not survive contact with this codebase, because it is not the stance the project takes at its other two extension points:

- `EnrichmentProvider` is public and consumer-registrable via `addProvider`. A provider that throws is caught at *both* chain call sites and converted to `EnrichmentResult.Error(type, provider.id, message, cause)`. A throwing provider is equally "the consumer's bug", and it is emphatically not propagated.
- `EnrichmentCache` is public and consumer-implementable. v0.10.0 guarded it (#22).

That leaves mergers and synthesizers as the sole unguarded consumer extension point out of three. The inconsistency is the argument, and it also answers the design question: guard by *reporting*, not by silently degrading. The cache precedent (degrade to a miss, log, carry on) does not transfer — the cache is an optimisation, whereas a merger produces the result for its type, so a swallowed failure would be indistinguishable from a genuine `NotFound`.

The second wontfix argument is that README on `dev` already documents the current behaviour. It does — but read the change that put it there. The #22 commit describes it as narrowing README "to what the code actually guarantees", landed in the same PR that fixed the cache. That is a known-limitation note written under scope discipline, not a design decision blessing the gap. README's headline promise in that same section is still "The engine never throws from `enrich()`", and ROADMAP's core principles still lead with "Resilient by default". Closing this deletes the carve-out rather than contradicting a guarantee.

**Why not `bug`.** #22 was a bug because README promised cache coverage the code did not deliver — a doc/code mismatch. Here doc and code agree; nothing is broken relative to the stated contract, and no stock path can trigger it. It is hardening of a documented gap, so `enhancement` is the honest category. Flagging the swap explicitly rather than silently relabelling.

**Current behavior:**
A `ResultMerger.merge()` or `CompositeSynthesizer.synthesize()` that throws propagates the exception out of `enrich()`. All results for all requested types — including cache hits and already-completed provider work — are discarded.

**Desired behavior:**
A throwing merger or synthesizer yields `EnrichmentResult.Error` for *that type only*, carrying the exception as `cause` and a provider string identifying the failing strategy. Every other requested type resolves and returns normally. `enrich()` does not throw.

**Key interfaces:**
- `ResultMerger.merge()` / `CompositeSynthesizer.synthesize()` — public interfaces, signatures unchanged. Only the engine's invocation of them changes.
- `EnrichmentResult.Error(type, provider, message, cause, errorKind)` — the conversion target. Attach the throwable as `cause`; `ErrorKind.UNKNOWN` is the right kind (an engine-side strategy fault is none of NETWORK/AUTH/PARSE/RATE_LIMIT, and TIMEOUT is reserved for deadline expiry).
- `CancellationException` must be rethrown, never converted — same rule the cache guard follows, and here it is load-bearing twice over, since the enrichment deadline and sibling-cancellation both surface that way.
- No public API change. `apiCheck` must stay green and `api/*.api` must be untouched — the guard belongs in `internal` engine code.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] A registered `ResultMerger` whose `merge()` throws produces `Error` for its own type; `enrich()` returns normally and every other requested type carries its real result.
- [ ] Same for a `CompositeSynthesizer` whose `synthesize()` throws.
- [ ] The returned `Error` exposes the original throwable via `cause`, so the consumer can diagnose their own strategy.
- [ ] A throw in one merger does not cancel or discard concurrently-resolving sibling types, nor drop results already served from cache.
- [ ] `CancellationException` from a merger or synthesizer still propagates — a cancelled or timed-out caller stops the work.
- [ ] Regression tests cover both extension points, using fakes in the established `testutil/` style.
- [ ] `apiCheck` green with `api/*.api` unmodified.
- [ ] README's extension-point carve-out is removed or rewritten, since it will no longer be true. CHANGELOG updated.

**Out of scope:**
- Changing the `ResultMerger` / `CompositeSynthesizer` signatures, or adding a result-returning error channel to them. The engine catches; the interfaces stay as they are.
- Rewriting the built-in mergers or synthesizers. All eight were audited during triage and none can throw on current inputs.
- Restructuring the fan-out's `coroutineScope` / `awaitAll` shape, or making regular-type resolution survive independently of the merge phase. The guard keeps the throw from ever reaching the scope, which is sufficient.
- Touching the cache guard from #22.

**References (current code at time of triage — may shift):**
- `musicmeta-core/src/main/kotlin/com/landofoz/musicmeta/engine/DefaultEnrichmentEngine.kt` — `resolveTypes()`, the merge `async` block and the composite-synthesis loop; and `enrich()`, whose sole `catch` is `TimeoutCancellationException`
- `musicmeta-core/src/main/kotlin/com/landofoz/musicmeta/engine/ProviderChain.kt` — the exception→`Error` conversion to mirror, present in both `resolveAll()` and `forEachEligible()`
- `musicmeta-core/src/main/kotlin/com/landofoz/musicmeta/engine/CacheGuard.kt` — structural precedent for a small `internal` guard helper in its own file, including the `CancellationException` rethrow and its rationale. `DefaultEnrichmentEngine.kt` is already over the 300-line CLAUDE.md ceiling, so a new file is the precedent for a reason.
- `musicmeta-core/src/test/kotlin/com/landofoz/musicmeta/engine/EnrichCacheFailureTest.kt` — test precedent for "throwing consumer component does not break `enrich()`"
- `41a4460` / #22 / v0.10.0 CHANGELOG "Fixed" entry — the analogous fix and its reasoning
Landed via #32 (squashed into dev).

issues.title: Validate release version agreement before the tag exists, not only after
issues.body:
## Problem

Publication is tag-triggered: pushing a `v*` tag fires `publish.yml`, and its guards — the version-match assertion (#13/#31) and `apiCheck` — necessarily run **after** the tag exists. This is inherent to the tag-as-trigger model, not a bug. But it means the failure modes those guards catch are only caught once there is already an immutable tag, so recovery is "delete and re-push the tag."

`publish.yml` documents this deliberately ("the LAST line of defence, not the first"). #31 already closed the genuinely dangerous version — publish.yml deriving nothing from the tag and silently uploading the wrong GAV. What remains is a recoverable-but-annoying gap: a tag can exist for a version that then fails to publish.

Two things make that gap worth narrowing:

1. **Version drift is knowable before any tag.** All three modules declare `version` independently in their `build.gradle.kts` and can drift from each other or from the pinned `CHANGELOG` heading. Nothing asserts they agree until a tag is pushed.
2. **Transient infra fails post-tag.** The publish job runs tests + `apiCheck` after the tag exists; the workflow comments name the Robolectric/Maven CDN hiccup. A flaky runner therefore forces a delete-and-re-push for a reason unrelated to the release being wrong.

## Proposed fix (cheap version)

Add a release-readiness assertion that runs **before** the tag — on the release PR (`dev` → `main`) in `build.yml`, or as a small dispatchable check:

- All three module versions (`musicmeta-core`, `musicmeta-android`, `musicmeta-okhttp`) equal **each other**.
- They match the version pinned at the top `## [x.y.z]` heading of `CHANGELOG.md`.

No tag is needed — it reads the declared versions from Gradle (as #31's guard does) and the pinned CHANGELOG heading. By tag time the version-match guard in `publish.yml` is then already known-green, so the "immutable tag for an unpublished version" state cannot arise from version mismatch. Keep the `publish.yml` guard as the backstop.

## Fuller alternative (not proposed here)

Invert the trigger entirely: `workflow_dispatch` with the version as input → verify → test → publish → **create the tag last** on success (`contents: write`). This makes the bad state structurally impossible — the tag becomes a record of a successful publish rather than a trigger for an attempted one — but it rewrites the release trigger and is a larger change than the gap warrants today. Recorded as the option, not the recommendation.

## Non-goals

- Collapsing the three independent version declarations to a single source (tracked separately per #31's commit message).
- Removing the `publish.yml` guards — they stay as the last line of defence.
comments:
Landed on `dev` via #36 (squash `87cb9d4`). The `release-readiness` job in `build.yml` now asserts the three module versions agree with each other and the pinned CHANGELOG heading on the `dev` → `main` release PR, before any tag exists.

Follow-ups filed: #37 (collapse the three version declarations to a single source — the stronger structural fix) and #38 (promote this check to a required status check on `main`'s ruleset, once it has run on a `main`-targeted PR).

issues.title: Collapse the three module version declarations to a single source
issues.body:
## Problem

The three modules — `musicmeta-core`, `musicmeta-android`, `musicmeta-okhttp` — each declare `version` independently in their own `build.gradle.kts`. Nothing structurally prevents them drifting from each other; a release requires editing the same version string in three places and keeping them in sync by hand. This has already been a live footgun (the 0.10.0 release had mismatched declarations on `dev`, fixed by hand before merge — see #13 / #31).

Two guards now *detect* that drift:
- `publish.yml` asserts the pushed tag matches all three declared versions (#31, closes #13) — but only **after** an immutable tag exists.
- `build.yml`'s `release-readiness` job asserts the three agree with each other and with the pinned `CHANGELOG` heading on the `dev` → `main` release PR (#35 / #36) — **before** the tag.

Both detect a mismatch. Neither makes it **impossible**.

## Proposed change

Collapse the three declarations to a single source of truth — e.g. a `version` in the root `gradle.properties` (or the root `build.gradle.kts`) that all three modules inherit — so cross-module drift becomes **unrepresentable** rather than merely detected. The version would then be edited in exactly one place per release.

## Why it's filed separately

Called out as the stronger fix but deliberately deferred in #13's decision (`STORIES.md`, 2026-07-22): *"A shared `gradle.properties` value would make cross-module drift unrepresentable rather than merely detected... It also edits publishing configuration in all three modules — a high-risk surface — for a failure mode this guard already catches before it can reach Central. Wants its own issue and its own review."* Also named as a non-goal in #35.

## Scope / cautions

- Touches publishing configuration in all three modules — a **high-risk surface**. Per `docs/project/workflow.md` this needs explicit human approval and an independent review; not unattended P3 work.
- Verify the published Maven coordinates (GAV) are byte-for-byte unchanged after the refactor — the `api/*.api` baselines won't catch a version/coordinate regression.
- The existing detection guards (#31 in `publish.yml`, `release-readiness` in `build.yml`) stay as backstops.

## Non-goals

- Changing the publish trigger model (the `workflow_dispatch` → publish → tag-last inversion recorded in #35 is a separate option).
comments:
Landed on `dev` via #39 (squash `c96058c`). Closing explicitly — `dev` isn't the default branch, so the `Closes #37` keyword doesn't auto-close.

Version is now declared once in root `gradle.properties` and inherited by all three modules; the per-module `version` lines are gone. Verified: generated POMs byte-for-byte identical before/after (GAV unchanged), both version guards still read `0.10.1` for all three, full `./gradlew build` + demo composite build green in CI. `group` left per-module by design (see the STORIES entry).

issues.title: Make the release-readiness check required on main's ruleset
issues.body:
## Problem

#35 / #36 adds a `release-readiness` job to `build.yml` that runs on the `dev` → `main` release PR and fails if the three module versions disagree with each other or with the pinned `## [x.y.z]` `CHANGELOG` heading. It was deliberately shipped as an **advisory** check, not a required one — its value today is the red X a human reviewing the release PR sees.

But the live `main` ruleset requires only the `build` context, so a red `release-readiness` blocks nothing: the release PR can still be merged with the check failing. Enforcement is left to whoever remembers to look.

## Proposed change

Add `release-readiness` to the required status checks in `main`'s branch ruleset, so a version mismatch **blocks** the release PR merge rather than merely flagging it.

Safe to require:
- The job only runs on `pull_request` with `base_ref == main`, so it gates release (and hotfix/docs) PRs into `main` and nothing else.
- A docs-only PR into `main` (the deferred-tagging exception in `release.md`) leaves versions and heading untouched, so it passes — requiring it doesn't block that path.

## Notes

- This is a **repo settings / ruleset** change (admin), **not** a code change — no PR implements it.
- **Depends on #36 merging first** — the `release-readiness` context must exist on a `main`-targeted PR before it can be added as a required check.
- Related: #35 (the check), #31/#13 (the post-tag backstop it front-runs), #37 (the stronger structural fix).
comments:
Done via repo settings — no PR (this is a ruleset change, as noted in the issue).

Added \`release-readiness\` to the **main protection** ruleset's required status checks. It now requires both contexts:

- \`build\`
- \`release-readiness\`

Ruleset unchanged otherwise: still `active`, still targets `refs/heads/main` only, "require branches up to date" still on. The `release-readiness` job runs on every `pull_request` with `base_ref == main` (its `if:` guard), so it always reports on the PRs this ruleset gates — no risk of a stuck "expected" check. A docs-only PR into `main` leaves the versions and pinned `## [x.y.z]` heading untouched, so it passes green and the deferred-tagging path stays unblocked.

Depended on #36 (merged). Related: #35 (the check), #31/#13 (the post-tag backstop it front-runs), #37 (the structural fix, now open as a PR).

issues.title: DefaultEnrichmentEngine takes an httpClient it never uses
issues.body:
`DefaultEnrichmentEngine` declares `private val httpClient: HttpClient` as its third constructor parameter and never uses it. The name appears exactly once in the file — its own declaration.

Surfaced by detekt (`UnusedPrivateProperty`) when static analysis was added in #47, and baselined there rather than fixed, because the fix is a public API break.

## Impact

**Not a correctness bug.** Providers get their HTTP client from a different path — `Builder.withDefaultProviders()` resolves `val client = httpClient ?: DefaultHttpClient(config.userAgent)` and passes it to every provider, so `Builder.httpClient(myClient)` behaves as a consumer expects.

The waste is in `Builder.build()`:

```kotlin
return DefaultEnrichmentEngine(
    registry = registry,
    cache = cache ?: InMemoryEnrichmentCache(),
    httpClient = httpClient ?: DefaultHttpClient(config.userAgent),   // <- second instance
    ...
)
```

This re-evaluates the elvis rather than reusing the `client` built in `withDefaultProviders()`, so when no custom client is supplied **every `build()` allocates a second `DefaultHttpClient` that nothing ever touches**. Harmless at runtime — it opens no connections — but it is a dead object and a dead parameter in the published ABI.

## Why this is a breaking change

The constructor is in the committed baseline:

```
public fun <init> (Lcom/landofoz/musicmeta/engine/ProviderRegistry;Lcom/landofoz/musicmeta/EnrichmentCache;Lcom/landofoz/musicmeta/http/HttpClient;Lcom/landofoz/musicmeta/EnrichmentConfig;Lcom/landofoz/musicmeta/EnrichmentLogger;Ljava/util/List;Ljava/util/List;)V
```

`HttpClient` is the 3rd of 7 parameters. Removing it shifts every positional argument after it — a source break for direct callers, and a binary break for pre-compiled ones since the JVM descriptor changes. Consumers exist on Maven Central and JitPack.

Per the 0.x carve-out in `CLAUDE.md`, a minor release may carry this, but it must appear under `### Breaking Changes` in `CHANGELOG.md` and be visible in the reviewed `api/*.api` diff.

## Options

1. **Remove the parameter.** Cleanest. Breaking; needs a `0.x.0` and a CHANGELOG entry. Touches ~35 test call sites plus the Builder.
2. **Make `DefaultEnrichmentEngine` internal first.** `CLAUDE.md` already flags it as engine wiring that is public by omission and due a visibility pass, alongside `ProviderRegistry` and `ConfidenceCalculator`. The Builder is the intended entry point. Doing this removes the question entirely — the constructor stops being public API and the parameter can go without ceremony. Still breaking, but it breaks something that arguably should never have been reachable.
3. Reuse `client` in `build()` and keep the parameter. Removes the wasted allocation, keeps the dead parameter. Non-breaking but leaves the actual defect.

Option 2 looks like the better trade if a visibility pass is happening anyway — one break instead of two.

## Acceptance

- No unused constructor parameter on `DefaultEnrichmentEngine`
- `Builder.build()` does not construct an `HttpClient` it discards
- Baseline entry removed from `config/detekt-baseline-musicmeta-core.xml` (not re-baselined)
- Any signature change documented under `### Breaking Changes` and reflected in the `api/*.api` diff
comments:
## Triage: fixed on an in-flight PR, not yet merged

Re-verified against `docs/claude-md-pointers` (the head of open PR #75). All four acceptance
bullets are already met on that branch:

- `DefaultEnrichmentEngine` is now `internal` and its constructor is `(registry, cache, config,
  logger, mergers, synthesizers)` — no `httpClient` parameter. This is Option 2 followed by
  Option 1, which is what the body recommended.
- `Builder.build()` no longer re-evaluates `httpClient ?: DefaultHttpClient(...)`; it passes
  `registry`, `cache`, `config`, `logger`, `mergers`, `synthesizers` only. The second discarded
  `DefaultHttpClient` per `build()` is gone.
- The `UnusedPrivateProperty` entry for `DefaultEnrichmentEngine` is no longer in
  `config/detekt-baseline-musicmeta-core.xml` (the two remaining entries are both test files).
- The break is under `### Breaking Changes` and visible in the `api/musicmeta-core.api` diff
  (54 lines removed), and PR #75 states the next release must be `0.11.0`.

**Not closing yet — PR #75 is open, and its body carries no `Closes #48`,** so this will not
auto-close on merge. Close it manually when #75 lands, or add the keyword to the PR body.

No further work needed here.

issues.title: addMerger for ARTIST_TOP_TRACKS is silently overridden by the built-in
issues.body:
`Builder.addMerger()` is public API, but a merger registered for `ARTIST_TOP_TRACKS` is silently discarded.

## Mechanism

`EnrichmentEngine.kt:151` appends the built-in last:

```kotlin
val allMergers = mergers + TopTrackMerger
```

`DefaultEnrichmentEngine.kt:38` then keys them:

```kotlin
private val mergers: Map<EnrichmentType, ResultMerger> = mergers.associateBy { it.type }
```

`associateBy` keeps the **last** value for a duplicate key, and `TopTrackMerger.type` is `ARTIST_TOP_TRACKS` (`engine/TopTrackMerger.kt:20`). So:

```kotlin
EnrichmentEngine.Builder()
    .withDefaultProviders()
    .addMerger(myTopTracksMerger)   // dropped
    .build()
```

The consumer's merger never runs. No warning, no error — `addMerger` returns `this` and the call looks like it worked.

## Why it matters

`addMerger` is in the committed ABI (`musicmeta-core.api`), and `ResultMerger` is one of the two documented extension points that survived the v0.10.0 visibility narrowing specifically so consumers could use them. An extension point that silently ignores registrations is worse than one that does not exist.

Only `ARTIST_TOP_TRACKS` is affected today, because `TopTrackMerger` is the only merger appended after the caller's. The other built-ins (`GenreMerger`, `ArtworkMerger`, `SimilarArtistMerger`, `SimilarTrackMerger`) are seeded into the `mergers` list *before* `addMerger` runs, so a consumer override of those wins — which makes the behaviour inconsistent as well as wrong.

## Options

1. **Seed `TopTrackMerger` with the other built-ins** in the `Builder`'s initial list rather than appending it in `build()`. Smallest change, makes every built-in overridable the same way, no API change.
2. **Reverse the fold** — `allMergers.reversed().associateBy { it.type }`, or `associateBy` on a list with caller mergers last. Same effect, less obvious to a reader.
3. **Reject duplicates loudly** — throw or log on a second merger for one type. Safer but a behaviour change for anyone currently relying on override-wins for the other four.

Option 1 looks right: it makes the rule "the caller's merger wins" true for all five, which is what the other four already do.

## Acceptance

- A merger registered via `addMerger` for `ARTIST_TOP_TRACKS` is the one that runs
- Behaviour is consistent across all built-in merger types
- A test covers override for at least `ARTIST_TOP_TRACKS` and one other type
comments:
## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** A `ResultMerger` registered via `Builder.addMerger()` for `ARTIST_TOP_TRACKS` is silently discarded because the built-in `TopTrackMerger` is appended *after* the caller's mergers and last-wins de-duplication keeps the built-in.

**Verified mechanism (traced on `main`):**
- `EnrichmentEngine.Builder` seeds four built-ins into its `mergers` list at construction: `GenreMerger` (`GENRE`), `SimilarArtistMerger` (`SIMILAR_ARTISTS`), `SimilarTrackMerger` (`SIMILAR_TRACKS`), and two `ArtworkMerger` instances (`ARTIST_PHOTO`, `ALBUM_ART`). `addMerger()` **appends** the caller's merger to that same list — so for these five types the caller's entry lands *after* the built-in.
- `build()` then does `val allMergers = mergers + TopTrackMerger` — the fifth built-in, `TopTrackMerger` (`type == ARTIST_TOP_TRACKS`), is appended **after** everything, including any caller merger.
- `DefaultEnrichmentEngine` folds the combined list with `mergers.associateBy { it.type }`, and `associateBy` keeps the **last** value per key. So the caller wins for the four seeded types (their entry is later than the built-in) but **loses** for `ARTIST_TOP_TRACKS` (the built-in is appended last). No warning; `addMerger` returns `this` and the registration silently no-ops.

**This is a bug, not a deliberate "built-in wins" contract:** neither `addMerger()` nor the `ResultMerger` interface documents any precedence rule, and the four-win/one-lose asymmetry is a direct artifact of *where* `TopTrackMerger` is added (in `build()` rather than the seed list), not a design choice. The reporter is the maintainer/author; the recommended fix (Option 1) and the acceptance criteria below are treated as the live spec.

**Desired behavior:** "the caller's merger wins" holds for **all five** built-in merger types, including `ARTIST_TOP_TRACKS`. With no override registered, behavior is unchanged (the built-in still runs).

**Contract:**
- A merger registered via `addMerger` for any built-in type — including `ARTIST_TOP_TRACKS` — is the one that runs; the built-in is the fallback only when the caller registers nothing for that type.
- Behavior is consistent across all five built-in merger types.

**Recommended fix (Option 1):** seed `TopTrackMerger` into the `Builder`'s initial `mergers` list alongside the other built-ins, so it is subject to the same seeded-first / caller-appended-last ordering. `build()` then no longer appends it. Smallest change, purely internal wiring.
- Option 2 (reverse the fold) reaches the same result but is strictly less readable — dominated by Option 1.
- Option 3 (reject duplicates loudly) is *rejected*: it contradicts acceptance criterion 1 (the override must **run**, not throw) and is a breaking behavior change for any consumer currently relying on override-wins for the other four types.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] A `ResultMerger` registered via `addMerger` for `ARTIST_TOP_TRACKS` is the merger that runs (the built-in `TopTrackMerger` does not shadow it).
- [ ] Override-wins behavior is identical across all five built-in merger types.
- [ ] With no override registered, `ARTIST_TOP_TRACKS` still resolves through the built-in `TopTrackMerger` (no regression to the default path).
- [ ] Regression test covers override for at least `ARTIST_TOP_TRACKS` **and** one other built-in type (e.g. `GENRE`).
- [ ] **`api/musicmeta-core.api` is unchanged** — the fix is internal wiring only. `addMerger(ResultMerger): Builder` is committed ABI (`musicmeta-core.api:978`) and must keep its signature; `mergers` is private and the `DefaultEnrichmentEngine` constructor is untouched. Per the "0.x carve-out" in `CLAUDE.md`, any `.api` diff here would be an unintended break and a defect.

**Out of scope:**
- Changing `addMerger`/`ResultMerger` public signatures or visibility.
- Adding duplicate-detection/rejection semantics (Option 3) — explicitly rejected above.
- Reworking how synthesizers (`addSynthesizer`) are folded — different path, not part of this bug.

**References (current code at time of triage — may shift):**
- `musicmeta-core/.../EnrichmentEngine.kt` — `Builder` merger seed list (~L93-97), `addMerger` (~L109), `build()`'s `mergers + TopTrackMerger` (~L151).
- `musicmeta-core/.../engine/DefaultEnrichmentEngine.kt` — `mergers.associateBy { it.type }` (~L40).
- `musicmeta-core/.../engine/TopTrackMerger.kt:20` — `type == ARTIST_TOP_TRACKS`.
- `musicmeta-core/api/musicmeta-core.api:978` (addMerger), `:2036` (ResultMerger public interface).
- Filed by commit b1f770ea ("Found on the way and filed rather than fixed here: #48, #49, #50"); no prior fix PR exists.
## Triage re-verification (2026-07-26)

The Agent Brief above still holds exactly as written. Re-traced on `docs/claude-md-pointers`:

- `EnrichmentEngine.Builder` seeds five built-in merger instances (`GenreMerger`,
  `SimilarArtistMerger`, `SimilarTrackMerger`, and two `ArtworkMerger`s) into `mergers`;
  `addMerger` appends after them.
- `build()` still does `val allMergers = mergers + TopTrackMerger` — the sixth built-in appended
  last, after any caller merger.
- `DefaultEnrichmentEngine` still folds with `mergers.associateBy { it.type }`, which keeps the
  last value per key.

So the four-win / one-lose asymmetry is unchanged and the recommended fix (seed `TopTrackMerger`
alongside the others, drop the `+ TopTrackMerger` in `build()`) is still the smallest change.

One correction to the brief's wording: `DefaultEnrichmentEngine` is now `internal` on PR #75's
branch, so the acceptance bullet "`api/musicmeta-core.api` is unchanged" is easier to hold than
when it was written — the engine constructor is no longer in the baseline at all. `addMerger` and
`ResultMerger` remain public and must keep their signatures.

Stays `ready-for-agent`.
## Correction: the brief's counts are off by one, and one of them is in an acceptance criterion

Missed in the re-verification above. The Agent Brief says the caller wins for "the four seeded
types" and asks for behaviour consistent "across all five built-in merger types". Both are one low.

`Builder` seeds five merger **instances** covering five **types**:

| Instance | Type |
|---|---|
| `GenreMerger` | `GENRE` |
| `SimilarArtistMerger` | `SIMILAR_ARTISTS` |
| `SimilarTrackMerger` | `SIMILAR_TRACKS` |
| `ArtworkMerger(ARTIST_PHOTO)` | `ARTIST_PHOTO` |
| `ArtworkMerger(ALBUM_ART)` | `ALBUM_ART` |

`TopTrackMerger` is the **sixth**, covering `ARTIST_TOP_TRACKS`. So the correct statement is: a
caller override wins for five types and loses for one, and there are six built-in merger types
in total.

This matters because it is load-bearing in the acceptance criteria, not just in the prose. An
implementer working from "all five built-in merger types" would assert override-wins across five and
believe they had covered the surface, leaving the sixth — the one this issue is actually about —
outside the criterion that was supposed to catch it. Read those two bullets as **six** and **five
win / one loses**.

Nothing else in the brief changes: the mechanism, the recommended fix (seed `TopTrackMerger`
alongside the other five, drop the `+ TopTrackMerger` in `build()`), and the rejection of
duplicate-detection all stand.

issues.title: One RateLimiter is shared across eight providers, contradicting its own KDoc
issues.body:
`RateLimiter`'s own KDoc states the contract:

```kotlin
/**
 * Enforces a minimum interval between requests.
 * Each provider should have its own RateLimiter instance.
 */
```

`Builder.withDefaultProviders()` does the opposite. One `RateLimiter(100)` is created and handed to eight providers:

```kotlin
val defaultRateLimiter = RateLimiter(100)
addProvider(CoverArtArchiveProvider(client, defaultRateLimiter))
addProvider(WikidataProvider(client, defaultRateLimiter))
addProvider(WikipediaProvider(client, defaultRateLimiter))
addProvider(DeezerProvider(client, defaultRateLimiter, ...))
addProvider(ListenBrainzProvider(httpClient = client, rateLimiter = defaultRateLimiter, ...))
addProvider(LrcLibProvider(client, defaultRateLimiter))
// plus LastFm, FanartTv, Discogs when keys are supplied
```

Only MusicBrainz gets its own (`RateLimiter(1100)`, correctly — its 1 req/sec rule is a real API limit).

## Why it matters

`RateLimiter` serialises on a `Mutex` and enforces the interval globally to the instance. Shared across eight providers targeting eight *different hosts*, the fan-out no longer runs concurrently in the way the engine's design implies — `resolveTypes()` launches the chains under `coroutineScope { async { } }`, but they then queue behind one 100ms gate.

Worst case for a full fan-out touching all eight is ~800ms of pure serialisation, on the hot path, for no protocol reason: rate limits are per-host, and no host here asks to be throttled against another host's traffic.

This has not been reported as a bug, so it is filed as a correctness-of-intent issue rather than a regression — but the code contradicts its own documented contract, and the cost lands in the engine's main concurrency path.

## Questions to settle

- Was the sharing deliberate (one global politeness budget) or incidental? Nothing in git history or `CHANGELOG.md` records a decision.
- If deliberate, the KDoc is wrong and should say so.
- If incidental, each provider should get its own instance, and the per-host intervals should be chosen deliberately rather than all inheriting 100ms.

## Acceptance

- The code and the `RateLimiter` KDoc agree
- If per-provider instances land: a test asserting two providers with separate limiters do not serialise against each other
- If sharing is kept: the KDoc states the intent and the reason
comments:
Two notes from a docs-accuracy pass over `docs/` — both adjacent to this issue rather than new findings against it.

## The count is low: it is ten instances, not eight

`SimilarAlbumsProvider` is missing from the list. Its `DeezerApi` is built with the same instance:

```kotlin
val deezerApi = DeezerApi(client, defaultRateLimiter)   // EnrichmentEngine.kt:124
addProvider(SimilarAlbumsProvider(deezerApi))
```

Counting the `defaultRateLimiter` call sites in `withDefaultProviders()`: seven unconditional (Cover Art Archive, Wikidata, Wikipedia, Deezer, `SimilarAlbumsProvider` via `DeezerApi`, ListenBrainz, LRCLIB) plus three registered with keys (Last.fm, Fanart.tv, Discogs) — ten. The title says eight and the body lists nine.

This does not change the analysis, only widens it: `SIMILAR_ALBUMS` serialises on the same gate as everything else, and it is in `DEFAULT_ALBUM_TYPES`, so a plain `albumProfile()` call is affected.

## The provider docs already state a different number, and no issue covers that

Eight lines across three files document Last.fm and LRCLIB at 200ms:

- `docs/providers/README.md:39` — `| Last.fm | 5/sec | 200ms | Generous |`
- `docs/providers/README.md:42` — `| LRCLIB | Gentle | 200ms | |`
- `docs/providers/lastfm.md:11`, `:110`, `:129`
- `docs/providers/lrclib.md:11`, `:127`, `:139`

Neither `LastFmProvider` nor `LrcLibProvider` declares a constructor default for `rateLimiter`, so both take whatever is passed, and `withDefaultProviders()` passes the shared `RateLimiter(100)`. The shipped interval for both is 100ms. Last.fm's published limit is 5 req/s, so 200ms is the figure that matches the API and 100ms is twice that rate — for Last.fm the docs describe the safer setting and the code ships the looser one.

These eight lines are wrong today regardless of how this issue is resolved, but the fix belongs with it rather than ahead of it: the third question here — whether per-host intervals should be chosen deliberately instead of all inheriting 100ms — is exactly where Last.fm's 200ms would be settled. Correcting the docs to 100ms first would just have to be undone if per-provider instances land.

Suggest folding into acceptance: whichever way this goes, the per-provider docs state the interval each provider actually gets.
## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement (correctness-of-intent + docs accuracy)
**Summary:** One `RateLimiter(100)` instance is shared across ten providers targeting ten
different hosts, contradicting `RateLimiter`'s own KDoc and serialising the engine's fan-out on a
single mutex.

**Current behavior (re-verified 2026-07-26 on `docs/claude-md-pointers`):**
`Builder.withDefaultProviders()` creates `val defaultRateLimiter = RateLimiter(100)` and hands the
same instance to every provider except MusicBrainz. Counting call sites: Cover Art Archive,
Wikidata, Wikipedia, Deezer, `DeezerApi` (which backs `SimilarAlbumsProvider`), ListenBrainz and
LRCLIB unconditionally, plus Last.fm, Fanart.tv and Discogs when keys are supplied — **ten
providers, not the eight in the title or the nine in the body.** Only MusicBrainz gets its own
(`RateLimiter(1100)`, matching a real published 1 req/sec limit).

The pattern that decides who shares is worth naming, because it is the fix: `ITunesProvider`
declares `rateLimiter: RateLimiter = RateLimiter(3000)` and `withDefaultProviders()` calls
`ITunesProvider(client)` without passing one — so iTunes quietly gets its own instance. Every
provider that shares does so only because it declares no default and the Builder hands it one.

`RateLimiter` serialises on a `Mutex` and enforces its interval globally to the instance, so
`resolveTypes()`'s `coroutineScope { async { } }` fan-out queues behind one 100ms gate. `SIMILAR_ALBUMS`
is in `DEFAULT_ALBUM_TYPES`, so a plain `albumProfile()` call is affected.

**The docs already state a different number.** Eight lines document Last.fm and LRCLIB at 200ms —
`docs/providers/README.md:39,42`, `docs/providers/lastfm.md:11,110,129`,
`docs/providers/lrclib.md:11,127,139` — but neither provider declares a constructor default, so
both ship at 100ms. For Last.fm, 200ms is the figure that matches its published 5 req/s limit and
100ms is twice that rate: the docs describe the safer setting and the code ships the looser one.

**Desired behavior:** the code and the `RateLimiter` KDoc agree, and each provider's documented
interval is the interval it actually gets.

**Key interfaces:**
- `RateLimiter` — its KDoc states "Each provider should have its own RateLimiter instance."
- `EnrichmentEngine.Builder.withDefaultProviders()` — the ten call sites.
- Provider constructors (`LastFmProvider`, `LrcLibProvider`, …) — none declares a `rateLimiter`
  default, so all inherit whatever the Builder passes. `ITunesProvider` is the one that does, and
  is the shape to mirror if per-provider instances land.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] The code and the `RateLimiter` KDoc agree — either per-provider instances land, or the KDoc
      states the shared-budget intent and its reason.
- [ ] Every provider's documented interval in `docs/providers/` matches the interval it is
      constructed with.
- [ ] If per-provider instances land: a test asserting two providers with separate limiters do not
      serialise against each other.
- [ ] No regression in MusicBrainz's 1100ms gate — that one is a real published API limit and must
      stay its own instance.

**Out of scope:**
- Any mechanism that parses documented rate limits out of `docs/providers/` and matches them
  against `RateLimiter(...)` literals. That is a real parser and belongs in its own issue
  (#74 explicitly carves it out).

**References (current code at time of triage — may shift):**
- `musicmeta-core/.../EnrichmentEngine.kt:114-146` — `mbRateLimiter` / `defaultRateLimiter` and the
  ten call sites.
- `musicmeta-core/.../http/RateLimiter.kt` — the KDoc the code contradicts.

**Why this needs a human:**
Three unresolved questions, all contract calls. (1) Was the sharing deliberate — one global
politeness budget across the library — or incidental? Nothing in git history or `CHANGELOG.md`
records a decision. (2) If deliberate, the KDoc is what changes, not the code. (3) If incidental,
the per-host intervals should be *chosen* rather than all inheriting 100ms, and Last.fm's 200ms is
settled here rather than by correcting the docs to 100ms first — correcting them ahead of this
decision would just have to be undone.
## Missed in the brief: the obvious fix moves `api/musicmeta-core.api`

The brief above implies this is internal wiring. For one of the two candidate routes it is not, and
the difference is worth knowing before the decision rather than after the api dump moves.

Giving a provider a `rateLimiter` **default** is not free at the ABI. Kotlin emits a synthetic
constructor carrying the defaults bitmask, and `binary-compatibility-validator` records it.
Both shapes are already in the committed baseline:

```
# ITunesProvider — has defaults
public fun <init> (Lcom/landofoz/musicmeta/http/HttpClient;Lcom/landofoz/musicmeta/http/RateLimiter;I)V
public synthetic fun <init> (Lcom/landofoz/musicmeta/http/HttpClient;Lcom/landofoz/musicmeta/http/RateLimiter;IILkotlin/jvm/internal/DefaultConstructorMarker;)V

# LastFmProvider — no defaults, plain constructors only
public fun <init> (Ljava/lang/String;Lcom/landofoz/musicmeta/http/HttpClient;Lcom/landofoz/musicmeta/http/RateLimiter;)V
public fun <init> (Lkotlin/jvm/functions/Function0;Lcom/landofoz/musicmeta/http/HttpClient;Lcom/landofoz/musicmeta/http/RateLimiter;)V
```

So "give each provider its own sensible default, the way `ITunesProvider` already does" adds a
`public synthetic <init>` line per provider to the dump. That is **additive, not a break** — existing
callers still resolve — but it is a visible `.api` diff, and per `CLAUDE.md` a diff is reviewed
rather than absorbed.

**The cheaper route avoids it entirely:** construct distinct `RateLimiter` instances in
`Builder.withDefaultProviders()` and pass them positionally, exactly as the shared one is passed
today. Same runtime behaviour, no constructor signatures touched, no dump change at all. The
trade-off is that the chosen interval then lives in the Builder rather than next to the provider it
belongs to, where a reader of `LastFmProvider` would find it.

That is a real trade and it belongs in the third question this issue already asks — whether per-host
intervals should be chosen deliberately, and if so, where they should be *stated*. Worth settling in
the same decision rather than discovering at implementation time.

## Also worth noting: `ITunesProvider` is the counter-example, not an omission

It is the one provider that escapes the shared limiter, and not because the Builder treats it
specially — `withDefaultProviders()` calls `ITunesProvider(client)` with no limiter, and the
declared `RateLimiter(3000)` default takes over. Every provider that *does* share is sharing only
because it declares no default and accepts whatever it is handed. That is the mechanism behind the
whole defect, and it is also why the fix has the shape question above.

issues.title: Differential-test the convention gate's Kotlin scanner against KotlinLexer
issues.body:
`scripts/checks/check_conventions.py` decides whether every other piece of Kotlin in this repo is acceptable. Its `_code_mask()` classifies each character as code or comment/string-text; the three rules (`no !!`, `@Serializable` placement, file length) all consume that classification. **When the mask is wrong, the gate reports green while checking nothing.**

Four independent review rounds found seven such bugs, every one a silent false negative. They were caught by review, which does not scale and will not be repeated on the next rule anyone adds. This issue turns that into a mechanism: a differential test against the Kotlin compiler's own lexer.

## Why this earns its cost

Normally a 300-line script does not deserve a bespoke test harness. This one does:

- It is the **highest defect density in the repo** — seven bugs in ~150 lines of scanner logic.
- Its failures are **invisible**. A broken mask does not throw; it silently stops reporting violations, and `./check` still prints green.
- It **will keep changing**. Each new convention rule exercises the mask in a new way, and the current safety net is "four people reviewed it once".
- Two of the seven bugs were on shapes **already in the repo** — `WikidataApi.kt:33` has a nested quote inside a `${...}` template; a raw string ending in `"` would have hidden a `!!` anywhere after it.

## Prior art: this was already done once, by hand

The fourth review built exactly this harness ad hoc and used it to clear the current implementation. Results, for reference:

- **179/179 files** (100 main + 63 test + 16 demo), byte-exact agreement, every character position compared — not sampled
- **200/200 generated Kotlin programs** that compile clean, with every `!!` position known by construction; the gate reported exactly the planted lines
- **~157,000 enumerated delimiter strings**; every disagreement was on source that does not compile, each proven with `kotlinc` rather than asserted
- One apparent disagreement was a **bug in the oracle**, not the scanner (a lone `\r` lexes as `BAD_CHARACTER`)

That harness was thrown away with the agent's worktree. This issue is to rebuild it as a permanent, runnable part of the repo.

## The mutation suite — the most important part of this issue

A harness that has never been proven to catch anything is worth nothing. The ad-hoc version was validated by reintroducing each historical bug into `_code_mask()` and confirming the oracle caught it. **Rebuild this list; it is the harness's own test.** Numbers are files-caught out of the 179-file corpus:

| # | Mutation (reintroduce this defect) | Caught |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Raw string closes on the FIRST three quotes of a run, not the last | 20/179 |
| 2 | Backtick-escaped identifiers not skipped | 61/179 |
| 3 | No escape handling inside normal strings | 8/179 |
| 4 | Template braces not tracked (`${list.map { it }}` mis-nests) | 7/179 |
| 5 | Char literals not skipped | 3/179 |
| 6 | Line comments run to EOF instead of EOL | 103/179 |
| 7 | Template contents treated as text rather than code | 52/179 |
| 8 | Block comments do not nest | **0/179** — see below |

**Mutation 8 survives the corpus.** No file in this repo contains a nested block comment, so the corpus alone cannot catch it. It must be covered by a synthetic probe. This is the single most valuable fact in this issue: it proves corpus-only differential testing is insufficient, and the harness needs both a real-corpus pass *and* a construct probe suite.

## Verified starting facts

- `org/jetbrains/kotlin/lexer/KotlinLexer.class` and `KtTokens.class` are inside `kotlin-compiler-embeddable-2.1.0.jar`.
- That jar is **already present** in `~/.gradle/caches/modules-2/files-2.1/org.jetbrains.kotlin/kotlin-compiler-embeddable/2.1.0/`, arriving transitively with the Kotlin Gradle plugin. It is not declared in `gradle/libs.versions.toml`.
- Using the embeddable jar rather than a `kotlinc` CLI is deliberate: it pins the oracle to **exactly the Kotlin version that compiles this project** (2.1.0, from `libs.versions.toml`), so the lexer cannot drift from the real compiler, and there is no external prerequisite. The ad-hoc harness shelled out to a `kotlinc` it found inside an Android Studio plugin directory — do not copy that.
- Corpus today: 100 main + 63 test = **163 files, 1,168,940 bytes** (excluding `demo/`, which the gate does not scan). Largest single file `DefaultEnrichmentEngineTest.kt`, 71KB.

## Existing regression tests

`scripts/checks/test_check_conventions.py` has 35 tests; every historical bug has a named one (`test_double_bang_after_a_url_string_is_reported`, `test_raw_string_ending_in_a_quote_does_not_leak`, `test_backtick_identifier_with_an_apostrophe_does_not_leak`, and so on). Those stay. This harness is a **second, independent** check — the unit tests encode cases we thought of, the oracle finds the ones we did not.

## Scope

1. A JVM entry point that lexes a `.kt` file and emits token spans (`start end tokenType`), resolving `kotlin-compiler-embeddable` through Gradle rather than a hardcoded cache path.
2. A comparator that maps token types to code/text, runs `_code_mask()` over the same file, and reports byte-level disagreements with surrounding context.
3. A corpus mode (all 163 files) and a probe mode (synthetic constructs, mandatory — see mutation 8).
4. The mutation suite above, as the harness's own test.
5. Wiring: a step in `./check` plus a `make` target. The spike measured 0.23 s for the whole tree, so this gates on every push — no scheduled job needed.
6. A row in `ARCHITECTURE.md` under *Enforced by*, since it gates.

## Acceptance

- Running the harness on current `dev` reports **zero disagreements** on all 163 corpus files.
- All eight mutations are caught; mutation 8 is caught by the probe suite, and that is asserted, not assumed.
- The oracle resolves the Kotlin version from `libs.versions.toml` — bumping Kotlin must not silently leave the oracle on the old lexer.
- Nothing leaks into `api/*.api` (`apiCheck` runs inside `build`; a new module must not publish).
- `./check` still passes; the 35 existing tests still pass.
- A disagreement report names the file, byte offset, line, the two classifications, and the surrounding source — enough to act on without re-deriving it.

## Explicitly out of scope

- Per-character marker-splicing with a compile check. The coordinator proposed it; it is ~1.3M positions × one `kotlinc` run each and is not reachable. The lexer oracle subsumes it at token granularity. **Do not attempt it** — it is what made the fourth review run 85 minutes.
- Rewriting `_code_mask()`. It is currently believed correct; this is about keeping it that way.
- The other two checks (`@Serializable`, file length) beyond the mask they share.

---

# Spike results

A timeboxed spike answered the open questions. Everything below was measured or executed, not estimated.

## Working harness (verbatim — this compiles and runs)

Two jars are required on the classpath: `kotlin-compiler-embeddable` **and** `kotlin-stdlib`. Without stdlib you get `NoClassDefFoundError: kotlin/jvm/internal/markers/KMappedMarker` from `IElementType.<clinit>` — and `javac` compiles fine against the embeddable alone, so this only appears at runtime.

IntelliJ classes are **shaded**: `org.jetbrains.kotlin.com.intellij.*`, not `com.intellij.*`. Web examples will give you the latter and a class-not-found.

```java
import java.io.IOException;
import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
import java.nio.file.Files;
import java.nio.file.Path;

import org.jetbrains.kotlin.com.intellij.psi.tree.IElementType;
import org.jetbrains.kotlin.lexer.KotlinLexer;
import org.jetbrains.kotlin.lexer.KtTokens;

/** Prints "start end tokenTypeName" per token for each .kt file given on argv. */
public final class KtMask {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws IOException {
        KotlinLexer lexer = new KotlinLexer();
        for (String arg : args) {
            Path p = Path.of(arg);
            String src = new String(Files.readAllBytes(p), StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
            System.out.println("# " + p);
            lexer.start(src);
            for (IElementType t = lexer.getTokenType(); t != null; lexer.advance(), t = lexer.getTokenType()) {
                System.out.println(lexer.getTokenStart() + " " + lexer.getTokenEnd() + " " + t);
            }
        }
    }
}
```

No IntelliJ platform init is needed — no `Disposable`, no `CoreApplicationEnvironment`. `new KotlinLexer()` then `start()` just works.

## Token classification (corrected against the real `KtTokens`)

`KtTokens` exposes authoritative sets, but **neither is sufficient alone**:
- `KtTokens.COMMENTS.getTypes()` = `[BLOCK_COMMENT, EOL_COMMENT, SHEBANG_COMMENT, KDoc]`
- `KtTokens.STRINGS.getTypes()` = `[CHARACTER_LITERAL, REGULAR_STRING_PART]` — does **not** include quotes, escapes or template markers

**TEXT (not code):** `BLOCK_COMMENT`, `EOL_COMMENT`, `SHEBANG_COMMENT`, `DOC_COMMENT`, `OPEN_QUOTE`, `CLOSING_QUOTE`, `REGULAR_STRING_PART`, `ESCAPE_SEQUENCE`, `CHARACTER_LITERAL`, `SHORT_TEMPLATE_ENTRY_START`, `LONG_TEMPLATE_ENTRY_START`, `LONG_TEMPLATE_ENTRY_END`, `INTERPOLATION_PREFIX`, plus **`IDENTIFIER` whose first character is a backtick**.

**CODE:** everything else — `WHITE_SPACE`, keywords, operators, literals, plain `IDENTIFIER`, `FIELD_IDENTIFIER`, `DANGLING_NEWLINE`, `BAD_CHARACTER`.

Three corrections to the list the ad-hoc harness used:
- **`SHEBANG_COMMENT` was missing** — a `#!/usr/bin/env kotlin` first line would be scanned as code.
- **`INTERPOLATION_PREFIX` was missing** — new in Kotlin 2.1, for `$$"..."` strings.
- **`DOC_COMMENT.toString()` is `"KDoc"`**, so it cannot be matched by name. **Compare token types by identity against the `KtTokens` constants, never by `toString()`.** If the Java side emits labels for the Python comparator, emit a stable `TEXT`/`CODE`, not the raw `toString()`.

Two behaviours that make this easier than expected:
- **Backtick identifiers** lex as a single `IDENTIFIER` spanning the backticks. The lexer never looks inside, so a `//` in there cannot start a comment — but marking the token as *code* would let a naive scan fire inside it. Mark it text, detected by `src.charAt(tokenStart) == '`'`, not by token type.
- **`${...}` contents** are emitted as ordinary separate code tokens, including a fully nested `OPEN_QUOTE`/`REGULAR_STRING_PART`/`CLOSING_QUOTE` for a string inside a template. Nesting is handled for you, and the nested-string case that caused two of the seven historical bugs is correct by construction.

Implementer's call: whether the delimiters (`OPEN_QUOTE`/`CLOSING_QUOTE`, template start/end) are text or code. Either is defensible; the harness and `_code_mask()` must simply agree, and that decision belongs in one comment next to the token table.

## Timing — measured, so this can be a gate

171 files, 1,225,765 chars, 262,785 tokens, one JVM, JDK 21, three runs:

```
jvm_startup_ms=19  lex_ms=164  total_ms=224  per_file_ms=0.96
jvm_startup_ms=19  lex_ms=170  total_ms=229  per_file_ms=0.99
jvm_startup_ms=19  lex_ms=167  total_ms=233  per_file_ms=0.98
```

**~0.23 s wall for the whole tree, ~1 ms/file.** Cost is dominated by class-init of `KtTokens`/`IElementType` (~50 ms), not lexing. This is free — **put it in the every-push gate**, no separate scheduled job needed.

Do **not** fork one JVM per file: that turns 0.2 s into ~30 s.

## Packaging — recommended shape

Shell out to `java` from the Python comparator, with the classpath resolved by Gradle rather than hardcoded. Not a new subproject.

- A new `tools/` subproject lands in `settings.gradle.kts`, gets swept into `./gradlew build`, and inherits root conventions including `binary-compatibility-validator` — more to configure out of publishing than the job needs.
- A task inside `musicmeta-core` puts a compiler jar in a **published** module. Avoidable.

Files to change:
- `gradle/libs.versions.toml` — add `kotlin-compiler-embeddable = { module = "org.jetbrains.kotlin:kotlin-compiler-embeddable", version.ref = "kotlin" }`. It is currently **not declared**; it only reaches the cache transitively via the Kotlin Gradle plugin, which is not a contract to depend on. Using `version.ref = "kotlin"` is what keeps the oracle pinned to the compiler that builds the project.
- root `build.gradle.kts` — `configurations.create("ktLexer")`, a `dependencies { ktLexer(...) }` block for the embeddable plus stdlib, and `tasks.register("ktLexerClasspath") { doLast { println(configurations["ktLexer"].asPath) } }`. The root project is not published, so nothing reaches `api/*.api`.
- `scripts/checks/KtMask.java` (new) — the harness, emitting `start end TEXT|CODE`.
- `scripts/checks/test_code_mask.py` (new) — compile once into a cache dir, one JVM over all files, diff against `_code_mask()`.
- `check` — one step (note: `./check` and `Makefile` both exist on `dev` as of b1f770e; add a `make` target too).

## Gotchas that will bite the implementer

- **Classpath**: never hardcode `~/.gradle/caches/modules-2/...`. The hash directory is content-addressed and changes on any version bump, and CI may use a different `GRADLE_USER_HOME`. Use `./gradlew -q ktLexerClasspath`, cache the result, regenerate when `libs.versions.toml` is newer.
- **UTF-16 vs code points** — *the most likely source of a phantom mismatch*. Java offsets are UTF-16 units; Python indexes code points. They diverge on any astral-plane character (an emoji in a string literal or comment). Either assert BMP-only or normalise offsets on both sides.
- **CRLF**: the lexer counts both chars, but Python text mode silently collapses `\r\n` to `\n`, shifting every offset. Read binary on the Python side, or pass `newline=""`. No CRLF files exist today, so this would appear only after a `.gitattributes` change or a Windows contributor — i.e. mysteriously.
- **BOM**: survives on both sides and shifts offsets by one consistently, so it happens to work — but strip it on both sides or the first span looks wrong.
- **Fail loudly on an unknown token type** rather than defaulting it to CODE. `INTERPOLATION_PREFIX` (2.1), `RANGE_UNTIL`, `CONTEXT_KEYWORD` are all recent additions; `kotlin-compiler-embeddable` explicitly disclaims API compatibility. Failing loudly turns a future Kotlin upgrade into a one-line fix instead of a silent hole in the mask. This is the difference between a harness that decays and one that does not.

## A process note for whoever picks this up

Agent worktrees are cut from whatever base ref existed when they spawned, which may be stale. Two agents in this branch's history reported files as "missing" that existed on `dev`. Check `git -C <worktree> log --oneline -1` before believing a claim that something is absent.

## Residual risk the ad-hoc run did not cover

Carried over so it is not rediscovered: exhaustive enumeration beyond length 6 on the comment/char alphabet; short templates (`$name`) were asserted-equal rather than verified, harmless since a bare identifier cannot contain `!!`; `!!` inside a `${...}` inside a KDoc code fence had one hand probe only; non-UTF-8, BOM, and exotic line separators other than form feed are unexamined.

issues.title: Cancellation is swallowed on the provider path, recording circuit-breaker failures against healthy providers
issues.body:
## Summary

`CancellationException` is an `Exception`, and the provider path catches `Exception` broadly without rethrowing it. The result is not just a swallowed cancellation — it mutates circuit-breaker state, so **an `enrichTimeoutMs` expiry records failures against providers that never failed**, and repeated timeouts open circuits against healthy providers.

This is `CLAUDE.md` pitfall 2 reached through pitfall 5. `CLAUDE.md` currently asserts the guard already exists:

> every consumer-implementable interface needs one (`EnrichmentProvider`'s lives in `ProviderChain`)

It does not. There are exactly two `CancellationException` rethrows in the entire main tree — `engine/CacheGuard.kt:43` and `engine/StrategyGuard.kt:32`. That documentation claim is false and is part of what this issue fixes.

## The path

`DefaultEnrichmentEngine` wraps steps 2–6 in `withTimeout(config.enrichTimeoutMs)`. On expiry every in-flight `provider.enrich(...)` throws `CancellationException`. Then:

1. the provider's own `catch (e: Exception) { mapError(type, e) }` converts it to `EnrichmentResult.Error`, **or** `ProviderChain` does it at `ProviderChain.kt:39` (`resolveAll`) / `ProviderChain.kt:87` (`forEachEligible`);
2. `mapError` (`EnrichmentProvider.kt:64`) classifies it as `ErrorKind.UNKNOWN` — it has no `CancellationException` case;
3. `ProviderChain` reaches `is EnrichmentResult.Error ->` and calls `breaker?.recordFailure()`;
4. `CircuitBreaker.recordFailure()` increments `consecutiveFailures` and opens the circuit once it hits `failureThreshold`.

Structured concurrency still delivers the timeout to the caller — `DefaultEnrichmentEngine.kt:99` catches `TimeoutCancellationException` — so `enrich()` does not hang. **The damage is persistent breaker state**, which outlives the call: a provider that was merely slow, or was cancelled because a caller navigated away, accumulates consecutive failures and is eventually skipped entirely by `ProviderChain`'s eligibility check.

## Scale

- 38 broad `catch (… : Exception|Throwable)` sites in main sources; 18 files pair one with `suspend`
- `detekt`'s `TooGenericExceptionCaught` is disabled in `config/detekt.yml`, so nothing sees any of it today

## Fix

Root cause, not per-caller. Every provider catch funnels into `mapError()`, so one guard there covers ~35 sites:

```kotlin
fun mapError(type: EnrichmentType, e: Exception): EnrichmentResult.Error {
    if (e is CancellationException) throw e
    ...
}
```

plus the two `ProviderChain` sites, which catch on behalf of providers that do not catch internally. No signature changes, so `apiCheck` stays green.

Behaviour change worth noting in `CHANGELOG.md`: `mapError()` now throws on cancellation instead of returning an `Error`. That is the intent — a cancelled call must not look like a provider failure — but it is a behaviour change for any consumer calling `mapError` directly from a custom provider.

## Mechanism, so it does not come back

Add a rule to `scripts/checks/check_conventions.py`: a broad catch in a file containing `suspend` must either rethrow `CancellationException` or delegate to `mapError()`. Written before the fix it would need a 38-entry grandfather list, which is how a gate becomes decoration — so the fix lands first and the rule ships green.

Also add a row to `ARCHITECTURE.md` under *Enforced by*, and correct the false claim in `CLAUDE.md` pitfall 2.

## Acceptance

- A cancelled `enrich()` records **no** breaker failure — regression test at the `ProviderChain` level
- `mapError()` rethrows `CancellationException` rather than classifying it
- The custom rule is green on the fixed tree with no grandfather list
- `./check` passes; `apiCheck` green

issues.title: enrich() reports another component's withTimeout as its own TIMEOUT
issues.body:
Raised by an independent review during #53; **not verified beyond reading the code**, so confirm before fixing.
