`DefaultEnrichmentEngine.kt:99` catches `TimeoutCancellationException` to convert unfinished types into `Error(..., ErrorKind.TIMEOUT)`. That catch is by type, not by identity — it cannot tell the timeout created at `DefaultEnrichmentEngine.kt:77` from one thrown by anything else inside the block.

A custom `EnrichmentProvider`, `EnrichmentCache` or `CatalogProvider` that uses its own `withTimeout` internally, and lets it escape, is therefore reported to the caller as the engine's `enrichTimeoutMs` expiry. The consumer sees `ErrorKind.TIMEOUT` and reasonably concludes their `enrichTimeoutMs` is too low, when the real deadline was somewhere else entirely.

Suggested shape: `withTimeoutOrNull { ... }` returning a non-null sentinel on success, so only *that* lexical timeout produces the engine's TIMEOUT result and a foreign `TimeoutCancellationException` propagates as itself.

Worth checking whether any in-tree provider does this today — if none does, this is latent and only reachable by a consumer's implementation, which is why it is filed as p3 rather than fixed inside #53.
comments:
## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug (latent — reachable only through a consumer's own implementation)
**Summary:** `enrich()` catches `TimeoutCancellationException` by type, so a timeout thrown by
anything else inside the block is reported to the caller as the engine's `enrichTimeoutMs` expiry.

**Confirmed real (2026-07-26, `docs/claude-md-pointers`).** The body asked for verification before
fixing; here it is.

- `DefaultEnrichmentEngine.enrich()` opens `withTimeout(config.enrichTimeoutMs) { … }` and closes
  with `catch (_: TimeoutCancellationException)`. The catch discriminates on type alone — it cannot
  distinguish the exception its own `withTimeout` created from one that escaped a nested one.
- The catch then stamps every unfinished type as `Error(..., ErrorKind.TIMEOUT)` with the message
  "Enrichment timed out" and logs "Enrich timed out after ${config.enrichTimeoutMs}ms". Both are
  wrong when the deadline was somebody else's.
- The reachable path is a consumer's `EnrichmentProvider`, `EnrichmentCache` or `CatalogProvider`
  that uses `withTimeout` internally and lets the expiry escape. `EnrichmentProvider`'s own KDoc
  already acknowledges this shape ("a provider's own `withTimeout`"), as do `CacheGuard` and
  `StrategyGuard`.

**Still latent, which is why p3 is right.** No in-tree provider, cache or catalog implementation
calls `withTimeout` — grepped across `musicmeta-core`, `musicmeta-okhttp` and `musicmeta-android`;
every hit is either a comment or `enrich()`'s own. So today this is only reachable by consumer code.

**Desired behavior:** only `enrich()`'s own lexical deadline produces the engine's
`ErrorKind.TIMEOUT`. A `TimeoutCancellationException` originating anywhere else propagates as
itself, or is handled as the failure of the component that threw it — not relabelled as the
caller's `enrichTimeoutMs` being too low.

**Key interfaces:**
- `DefaultEnrichmentEngine.enrich()` — the `withTimeout` block and its `catch`.
- `ErrorKind.TIMEOUT` — what a consumer reads and acts on; this issue is about that signal lying.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] A `TimeoutCancellationException` thrown by a consumer-supplied provider/cache/catalog inside
      the enrichment block does **not** produce `ErrorKind.TIMEOUT` results attributed to `"engine"`.
- [ ] `enrich()`'s own deadline still produces `ErrorKind.TIMEOUT` for every unfinished type,
      unchanged.
- [ ] The existing invariant holds: a timeout must not discard results already fetched. Quoting the
      in-code comment — "Stale fallback and write-back are outside the withTimeout above on purpose:
      a timeout must not discard results already fetched. Don't move these inside the try."
- [ ] Regression test with a fake provider whose `withTimeout` expires inside the block.

**Out of scope:**
- The cache write-back question — that is #56, and see the sequencing note below.
- The `EnrichmentLogger` guard question — that is #71.

**References (current code at time of triage — may shift):**
- `musicmeta-core/.../engine/DefaultEnrichmentEngine.kt` — `withTimeout` at ~:77, `catch
  (_: TimeoutCancellationException)` at ~:99, write-back at ~:113-130.
- `search()` in the same file (~:160) shows the pattern already applied elsewhere: `ensureActive()`
  settles *this* job's cancellation and lets a foreign one fall through as the failure it is (#53).
  `enrich()`'s outer catch never got the equivalent treatment.

**Why this needs a human — sequencing, not design:**
The suggested fix shape (`withTimeoutOrNull` returning a non-null sentinel, so only that lexical
timeout produces the engine's result) is concrete enough to implement cold. But it restructures the
exact `withTimeout`/`catch` pair that **#56** is also about, and #56 has two open design questions —
one of whose candidate resolutions is "move catalog filtering out of the timed section entirely",
which changes what is inside this block. Landing this first risks rework.

The two are better read as one change: #56's likeliest fix needs a "we timed out" signal carried
out to the write-back, which sits outside the `withTimeout` and cannot see it today — and that
signal is precisely what the `withTimeoutOrNull` sentinel proposed here provides. Decide #56, then
land both together.

Fixed in #91 (commit a7fc80c): enrich() now uses withTimeoutOrNull with a success sentinel, so only the engine's own lexical deadline produces Error(TIMEOUT) and a foreign TimeoutCancellationException propagates as itself. Declared under Breaking Changes in [Unreleased]; the CatalogProvider escape path is documented in results-and-errors.md and pitfalls §6.

issues.title: Cache write-back can persist partially catalog-filtered results after a timeout
issues.body:
Raised by an independent review during #53; **not verified beyond reading the code**, so confirm before fixing.

`DefaultEnrichmentEngine` puts successful results into the map at `:94`, and the `TimeoutCancellationException` catch at `:99` deliberately preserves those already-collected successes. Write-back then runs at `:114`–`:125` and caches them.

`CatalogFilter.kt:107` suspends and mutates **one type at a time**. So if the deadline expires partway through filtering, the surviving results can be a mix of filtered and unfiltered types — and that mixture is what gets written to the cache, where it persists well beyond the cancelled call.

Two questions to settle, in order:

1. **Is partial success after the deadline intended at all?** Preserving collected successes on timeout looks deliberate. If so it should be documented on `enrich()`, because a consumer cannot currently tell a complete result from a truncated one.
2. **If it is intended, should partial results still be cached?** Caching a half-filtered set means the next call gets a hit and never re-filters. That is the part most likely to be a genuine bug rather than a documentation gap.

Related: #53 fixed cancellation being recorded as a provider *failure*. This is the other side — cancellation leaving a persistent artefact behind rather than a transient one.
comments:
## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug (with a documentation facet — see Q1)
**Summary:** A deadline that expires while catalog filtering is in progress leaves a mix of filtered and unfiltered recommendation results, and the write-back then caches that mix as if it were complete — so subsequent calls hit the cache and never re-filter.

**Trace confirms the mechanism (verified against code, not just prose):**
- Catalog filtering runs **inside** the `withTimeout` block. In `DefaultEnrichmentEngine.enrich()` the `withTimeout(config.enrichTimeoutMs)` lambda spans the identity/fan-out/filter section; `applyCatalogFiltering(...)` and identity-match stamping are the last two calls inside it, and the block closes immediately before the `catch (TimeoutCancellationException)`.
- `applyCatalogFiltering` (in `CatalogFilter.kt`) loops over `RECOMMENDATION_TYPES` and, for each type, makes a **suspending** `CatalogProvider.checkAvailability(...)` call, then replaces `results[type]` with the filtered result — one type at a time, mutating the shared map in place.
- If the deadline fires during a `checkAvailability` call, the exception propagates out of the loop with the map already carrying filtered entries for earlier types and still-unfiltered entries for the rest — a genuine mix.
- The timeout `catch` only fills in *missing* types with a `TIMEOUT` `Error`; it deliberately preserves everything already collected (both the filtered and the unfiltered successes).
- Write-back sits **outside** the timeout and caches every non-stale `Success`. The preserved successes have `isStale = false` and nothing marks them as truncated, so the half-filtered set is written to the cache under the primary (and possibly alias) key, where it survives the cancelled call. Next lookup is a hit and skips filtering entirely.

So the reporter's claim is **confirmed real**. It only manifests when a `CatalogProvider` is configured and `catalogFilterMode != UNFILTERED`, and the deadline lands in the (short) filtering window rather than during provider fan-out — but `checkAvailability` is itself a network/suspend call, so that window is reachable.

**Two open questions the maintainer posed (unresolved — this is why it needs a human):**
1. **Is partial success after the deadline intended at all?** The preserve-on-timeout behavior is deliberate (the `catch` fills only missing types). If it is the contract, it is currently undocumented on `enrich()` — the `EnrichmentEngine.enrich()` KDoc documents only `forceRefresh`, not what a timed-out `EnrichmentResults` contains, so a consumer cannot distinguish a complete result from a truncated one.
2. **If intended, should partial results still be cached?** This is the likely-genuine-bug half. Caching a half-filtered set poisons every future call for that key. Candidate resolutions differ materially and are a design call: (a) don't write back any result produced once the deadline expired (needs a "we timed out" signal carried to the write-back, since it currently sits outside the `withTimeout` and can't see it); (b) mark timed-out successes stale so the existing `!isStale` write-back guard already skips them; (c) only cache types that were fully filtered; (d) move catalog filtering out of the timed section so it always completes (trades one risk for another — filtering could then hang unbounded). Each has different blast radius and API-surface implications.

**Key interfaces:**
- `DefaultEnrichmentEngine.enrich()` — the `withTimeout` boundary and the write-back loop; the fix likely needs the write-back to know the run was truncated.
- `applyCatalogFiltering()` / `CatalogFilter.kt` — the per-type suspending mutation loop that a timeout can interrupt mid-way.
- `EnrichmentResult.Success.isStale` — the only field the write-back guard consults; option (b) would reuse it.
- `EnrichmentEngine.enrich()` KDoc — the surface Q1 would document.

**Acceptance criteria (once the design is chosen):**
- [ ] A timeout that fires mid-filter does not persist a mix of filtered and unfiltered recommendation results to the cache (assert via a fake `CatalogProvider` whose `checkAvailability` blocks past the deadline).
- [ ] Whatever the timeout contract is, it is stated on `enrich()` so a consumer can tell a complete result from a truncated one.
- [ ] Regression test covering the mid-filter-timeout path (the suite has `runTest` + fakes; mirror the cancellation tests added under #53).
- [ ] No regression in the intended "results survive a timeout rather than being discarded" behavior — the fix should stop *caching* the partial set, not stop *returning* it, unless the design explicitly decides otherwise.

**Out of scope:**
- The `CacheGuard`/`StrategyGuard` blanket-rethrow cleanup (that's #61).
- Broader rework of the timeout model beyond the cache-write-back question.

**References (current code at time of triage — may shift):**
- `musicmeta-core/src/main/kotlin/com/landofoz/musicmeta/engine/DefaultEnrichmentEngine.kt` — `enrich()`: `withTimeout` lambda (~:79–:100) contains `applyCatalogFiltering` (~:97); timeout `catch` (~:101); write-back loop (~:115–:129), outside the timeout.
- `musicmeta-core/src/main/kotlin/com/landofoz/musicmeta/engine/CatalogFilter.kt` — `applyCatalogFiltering` per-type suspending loop (~:102–:109), `checkAvailability` at ~:107.
- PR #54 (merged) / #53 — the sibling fix (cancellation recorded as a provider *failure*); this is the persistent-artefact side of the same family.

**Note on the docs:** the `ARCHITECTURE.md`/`CLAUDE.md` architecture map, step 6, states "Steps 2–6 sit inside `withTimeout`". That is imprecise in a way that matters here: catalog filtering and identity stamping are inside, but the `STALE_IF_ERROR` fallback and the cache write-back run **outside** the `withTimeout`. Whoever fixes this should correct that line while they are in the area — it is the exact boundary the bug turns on.

**Why this needs a human:** Both questions are unanswered design/product calls, not mechanical work. Q1 decides a public contract (what a timed-out `EnrichmentResults` promises) and Q2 chooses among several fixes with different API-surface and blast-radius implications. The maintainer explicitly filed this "confirm before fixing" with the two questions ordered and open; picking the resolution is the human's call, and the trace above is meant to make that call, not pre-empt it.
## Triage re-verification (2026-07-26)

The trace in the brief above still holds on `docs/claude-md-pointers`: `applyCatalogFiltering(...)`
and `stampIdentityMatch(...)` are the last two calls inside the `withTimeout` block, the
`TimeoutCancellationException` catch fills only *missing* types, and the write-back loop sits
outside the timeout and caches every `Success` with `!isStale`. The mid-filter mix can therefore
still be written to the cache under both the primary and the alias key. Confirmed real.

**One retraction.** The brief's closing "Note on the docs" asked whoever fixes this to correct an
`ARCHITECTURE.md`/`CLAUDE.md` line reading "Steps 2–6 sit inside `withTimeout`". That line no longer
exists — de1ddb2 ("docs: stop tracking the withTimeout boundary step-by-step in CLAUDE.md", #73)
removed it, and `ARCHITECTURE.md` has no `withTimeout` mention at all today. The boundary is now
documented where it belongs, as an in-code comment above the write-back. Ignore that paragraph.

**Sequencing.** #55 (a foreign `withTimeout` reported as the engine's own `ErrorKind.TIMEOUT`) is
the same change surface, not merely an adjacent one. Resolution option (a) here — don't write back
anything produced after the deadline — needs a truncation signal carried out to the write-back,
which sits outside the `withTimeout` and cannot see it. #55's proposed `withTimeoutOrNull`-plus-
sentinel restructure is exactly that signal. Deciding the two questions below settles #55's shape
too; they are best landed as one change.

Stays `ready-for-human` — both questions are still open and both are contract calls.

issues.title: CLAUDE.md pitfall 2 labels the cancellation regression as correct
issues.body:
Pitfall 2 in `CLAUDE.md` shows a `// RIGHT` code block containing:

```kotlin
catch (e: CancellationException) { throw e }
```

Twenty lines later the same pitfall states that exact form is wrong, and that `ensureActive()` is the correct guard because a `CancellationException` can also arrive from *inside* a provider whose own `withTimeout` expired.

An agent that reads the worked example and stops there writes the #53 regression. This is the false-rationale failure mode: a wrong config fails loudly, a wrong rationale in onboarding propagates silently and gets cited as precedent.

Two further doc claims are false against the repo as it stands:

- `ARCHITECTURE.md:65` says **46** pre-existing detekt findings sit in the baseline. `config/detekt-baseline-musicmeta-core.xml` contains **43**.
- `ARCHITECTURE.md:39` credits `./gradlew detekt` with enforcing "Kotlin complexity, dead code, bug patterns". The plain `detekt` task has no type resolution, so every type-requiring rule — `UnsafeCallOnNullableType`, `UnreachableCode`, `UnnecessaryNotNullOperator` — never runs. The register asserts an enforcement that does not happen.

Docs only. No code or config change.

issues.title: detekt runs without type resolution, so type-requiring rules never execute
issues.body:
Depends on #57

`./check` and `make lint` both run the plain `detekt` task, which has no type resolution. Every rule that needs a resolved classpath silently does nothing — `UnsafeCallOnNullableType`, `UnnecessaryNotNullOperator`, `UnreachableCode` and others. We have been running a linter that reports a subset it never discloses.

Measured with `detektMain` + `detektTest` across all three modules:

| | |
|---|---|
| total findings | **57** |
| breakdown | 35 `UseOrEmpty`, 20 `InjectDispatcher`, 2 `UnreachableCode` |
| failing tasks | `musicmeta-core` (main + test), `musicmeta-okhttp` (main) |
| clean | `musicmeta-android` |
| `UnsafeCallOnNullableType` / `UnnecessaryNotNullOperator` | 0 |

Four things this has to get right:

1. **It adds, it does not switch.** `./gradlew build --dry-run` shows `:musicmeta-core:detekt`, `:musicmeta-android:detekt` and `:musicmeta-okhttp:detekt` attached to Gradle `check`, which `build` depends on. Wiring `detektMain` into `./check` leaves the untyped task running later in the same command. Detach it or accept the duplication deliberately.
2. **`Makefile` must move too**, or `make lint` keeps running only the untyped task.
3. **Test-source `!!` policy becomes explicit.** detekt default config excludes `**/test/**` for `UnsafeCallOnNullableType`; `UnnecessaryNotNullOperator` has no such exclusion but does not fire on the 100 `!!` in our tests because they are on genuinely nullable receivers. Whichever way it lands, it should be a chosen line in `config/detekt.yml`, not an inherited default.
4. **Android SDK.** `detektDebug`/`detektRelease`, and therefore `detektMain`, require `ANDROID_HOME`. Plain `detekt` does not. `./check` already needs the SDK for `./gradlew build`, but `--fast` does not — this would put an SDK requirement, a Kotlin compile and a JVM start into the edit loop.

Accepted risk: type resolution in detekt 1.23.x is EXPERIMENTAL by every route — the predefined tasks, manual `classpath`/`jvmTarget` wiring, the CLI flags, and the compiler plugin. There is no stable option. Detekt 1.23.8 was also built against Kotlin 2.0.21 / AGP 8.8.1 while this repo is on Kotlin 2.1.0 / AGP 8.7.3, so every module task must be proven, not just core.

Keep `check_conventions.py` as-is in this issue. Deleting the `!!` rule depends on evidence produced here (see #60).

issues.title: Format-on-write hook misses every file written through Bash
issues.body:
The `PostToolUse` hook in `.claude/settings.json` matches `Edit|Write` only. Anything written through Bash — `sed -i`, a heredoc, a Python script — bypasses formatting entirely. This has already reached the gate: ktlint import-ordering failures from heredoc edits cost a full `./check` cycle to discover.

Adding `Bash` to the matcher does not fix it on its own. `scripts/format-kotlin.sh` reads `tool_input.file_path`; a Bash payload carries `tool_input.command` instead, so the script would exit silently and the hook would look fixed while doing nothing.

The fix has to enumerate what actually changed — `git status --porcelain` filtered to `*.kt`/`*.kts`, or a recent-mtime filter so a single Bash call does not reformat every modified file on the branch — or move to a `Stop` hook that sweeps once per turn.

Two constraints:

- **Cost sits in the write path.** The script already avoids Gradle for this reason. Whatever enumerates changed files has to be cheap enough to run after every Bash call, which argues for an early exit when nothing Kotlin changed.
- **Prove it with synthetic payloads.** Feed the script a fabricated Edit payload and a fabricated Bash payload and assert what it formats in each case. The current failure mode is precisely a hook that exits 0 while doing nothing, so "it did not error" is not evidence.

The script also swallows every formatter failure by design (`|| true`), because a file mid-edit may not parse. That stays — it makes this a convenience, not a guardrail, and `./check` remains the authority. Worth saying so in `ARCHITECTURE.md` rather than implying the hook enforces formatting.
comments:
Closing without a fix. The cure is worse than the disease, and I built two versions of it before that became clear.

**Attempt 1** widened the `PostToolUse` matcher to `Bash` and selected changed Kotlin by mtime inside a 30-second window. Review killed it: the window is not causally tied to the command. It misses a command that writes and then runs for a minute, misses anything preserving mtimes (`cp -p`, `rsync -t`, archive extraction), and grabs unrelated files another tool touched in the same moment. Its tests only confirmed the heuristic's own chosen examples.

**Attempt 2** dropped the heuristic for a `Stop` hook sweeping every dirty Kotlin file once per turn. That removed the attribution problem by removing attribution — and introduced a worse one:

- **It rewrites files it does not own.** `Stop` fires after *every* response, including a question-only turn. Someone with uncommitted work-in-progress who asks a question gets their WIP reformatted by a tool they did not invoke.
- **It desynchronises the index.** If a file is staged unformatted and the sweep formats the working copy, `ktlintCheck` passes against the working tree while the index still holds the unformatted version, and a later `git commit` records the stale copy.
- **It touches conflicted trees.** A mid-rebase or mid-merge tree reports `UU`/`AA`/`DU` entries, which it would hand to a formatter.
- **It runs after verification.** Formatting happens after the agent has already run `./check` and reported, so anything it changes is unverified by definition.

Causal attribution — "which files did *this* command write" — needs pre-turn state capture or transcript tracking. That is a real mechanism with real state, for a hook whose entire value is saving one `./check` cycle occasionally.

**So the gap stays, and it is recorded rather than papered over.** `PostToolUse` on `Edit|Write` keeps formatting files a payload names, which is the overwhelming majority of writes. Kotlin written through Bash is caught by `ktlintCheck` inside `./check`, which is what actually gates. That was always true; the hook only ever shortened the loop.

The generalisable lesson, which cost 326 lines of implementation and tests to learn: **the requirement that killed this design — "must not modify files the agent did not write this turn" — was knowable before any code.** Enumerating the states a change must not disturb (pre-existing dirt, staged content, conflicted trees, question-only turns) is a cheap pre-implementation step, and outside review ended up doing design validation after implementation instead.

Reopen if someone wants the transcript-tracking version and thinks it is worth the state.

issues.title: Retire the hand-written Kotlin scanner behind check_conventions.py
issues.body:
Depends on #58

`scripts/checks/` grew a Kotlin front end. `_code_mask()` (~155 lines) classifies every character of every `.kt` file as code or text so the convention rules can ignore comments and string literals. Seven silent bugs in it were the reason `KtMask.java` (118 lines, a `KotlinLexer` oracle) and `test_code_mask.py` (337 lines, a 195-file corpus plus an 8-mutation suite) exist. That layer reached ~1,379 lines of Python guarding ~10,300 lines of Kotlin, and it exists to defend a scanner we chose to hand-write.

The correct reading of "seven silent bugs in the masker" was not "build a compiler-lexer oracle" — it was "we accidentally started implementing a Kotlin front end; stop."

**Proof obligation before deleting anything.** Type-resolved detekt is not semantically equivalent to "ban every `!!`":

- `UnsafeCallOnNullableType` fires only when the receiver resolves as nullable.
- `UnnecessaryNotNullOperator` covers definitely non-null receivers.
- Neither is known to cover Java platform/flexible types — detekt 1.23.8 tests for `TypeNullability.NULLABLE`, excluding `FLEXIBLE`. `System.getProperty("x")!!` may pass both.

So run a mutation matrix first, in each module main source, through the **full** `./check` rather than one task, recording which rule rejects each cell:

| Cell | Mutation |
|---|---|
| nullable receiver | `val p: String? = null; p!!.length` |
| non-null receiver | `val p = "x"; p!!.length` |
| platform type | `val p = System.getProperty("musicmeta.probe")!!` |

If the platform cell passes, either keep a small syntactic ban or restate the invariant honestly as "no detekt-detectable `!!`". A zero-finding run is not evidence — with no `!!` in main sources today, zero is what you see whether the rule works or never runs.

**Scope, once that is settled.** Deleting only `check_no_double_bang()` changes nothing structural: the `@Serializable` placement check still calls `strip_noise()`, so the scanner, the oracle, the differential test and the `kotlin-compiler-embeddable` dependency all remain. The meaningful change is to replace the annotation check with a deliberately simple scan of `provider/` and `http/`, keep the trivial line-count rule, and delete `_code_mask`, `KtMask.java`, `test_code_mask.py`, the Gradle classpath plumbing and the related tests — roughly **-900 lines**.

What is *not* being concluded here: that custom rules are a bad idea. Small project-specific checks that no existing tool covers are worth keeping. What failed was owning a lexer.
comments:
Refuted by measurement in #63, before doing any of it.

The plan here assumed the `!!` rule was redundant under type-resolved detekt and could be deleted, leaving only the `@Serializable` check on `strip_noise()` — which a deliberately simple `provider/`/`http/` scan could replace, taking `_code_mask`, `KtMask.java` and `test_code_mask.py` with it. Two things kill that.

**1. The `!!` rule is not redundant.** Three-cell mutation matrix, run through the real gate in each main source:

| Mutation | detekt | `check_conventions.py` |
|---|---|---|
| `val p: String? = null; p!!.length` | ✅ `UnsafeCallOnNullableType` | ✅ |
| `val p = "x"; p!!.length` | ✅ `UnnecessaryNotNullOperator` | ✅ |
| `System.getProperty("musicmeta.probe")!!` | ❌ **neither rule** | ✅ |

A Java platform type passes both detekt rules — the check tests for `TypeNullability.NULLABLE`, and a flexible type is not that. Deleting the rule would have narrowed the invariant from "no `!!`" to "no detekt-detectable `!!`" without saying so, which is precisely the silent-scope-reduction this issue was written to avoid.

The original justification was that `detektMain` reported zero `UnsafeCallOnNullableType`. That was circular: there are no `!!` in main sources, so zero was the only possible result whether the rule worked or never ran.

**2. `check_no_double_bang` reads `strip_noise(source)`**, so keeping the rule keeps the scanner, and keeping the scanner keeps the differential test that stops it classifying code as text. The `@Serializable` check is not the only caller; simplifying it removes nothing.

So the ~-900 lines is not available. What is left would be deleting a `!!` gate that catches a case nothing else does, to remove a scanner that would still be needed — a net loss.

Closing as refuted rather than deferred. The generalisable part is recorded in `ARCHITECTURE.md` under *Not enforced*: detekt does not see `!!` on platform types, which is why that rule exists alongside it and not instead of it.

Standing correction to the reasoning that produced this issue: a zero-finding run is not evidence a tool covers what a hand-written check covers. Prove equivalence with one deliberate violation per semantic class, run through the full gate, and record which rule rejects each.

Reopening. My close reasoning was wrong, and a follow-up review caught it.

I argued: the mutation matrix proves the `!!` invariant must stay, `check_no_double_bang()` reads `strip_noise(source)`, therefore the scanner must stay. That conflates **the invariant** with **this implementation of it**. The matrix refutes deleting the *rule*. It says nothing about deleting the *lexer*.

Measured on `dev`:

```
$ grep -rn "!!" --include=*.kt musicmeta-*/src/main | wc -l
0
$ grep -rn "@Serializable" --include=*.kt \
    musicmeta-*/src/main/kotlin/com/landofoz/musicmeta/{provider,http} | wc -l
0
```

Zero literal `!!` in main sources **including comments and string literals**, and zero `@Serializable` under `provider/`/`http/` in any context. So a raw substring ban:

- passes today with no migration,
- enforces a *stronger* invariant than the masked version (a `!!` in a KDoc now fails too),
- and needs no code/text classification at all.

Which removes the entire reason `_code_mask()` exists, and with it `KtMask.java`, `test_code_mask.py`, the `ktLexer` configuration in `build.gradle.kts` and the `kotlin-compiler-embeddable` dependency.

The false positive that trade accepts is a genuine `!!` or `@Serializable` written inside a comment — for instance a comment explaining why `!!` is banned. Rare, loud, and one `# noqa`-style escape or a reworded comment away. `check_conventions.py` already states the principle it is decided by: *"a false positive is loud and a false negative is silent, and silent is the worse failure for a gate."* A substring ban is the same trade taken further, not a different one.

Revised scope:

- `check_no_double_bang` — substring scan, no `strip_noise`.
- `check_serializable_placement` — substring scan under `provider/`/`http/`, no `strip_noise`.
- file-length rule — already needs nothing.
- delete `_code_mask`/`strip_noise`, `KtMask.java`, `test_code_mask.py`, the `ktLexer` configuration and `ktLexerClasspath` task, and the scanner tests in `test_check_conventions.py`.
- `ARCHITECTURE.md` — drop the *"conventions scanner classifies Kotlin the way Kotlin does"* enforced row and the *"lexes Kotlin partially"* not-enforced entry; add the comment-false-positive trade as an accepted cost.
- `./check` loses its lexer-differential step, which also gives `--fast` back some of what it just lost to detekt.

Rough size: **~-900 lines**, and the remaining rules get *stricter*, not weaker.

Prerequisite unchanged: land #58 first, so the typed detekt rules are actually running when the scanner goes.

Blocked on nothing else. What I got wrong is worth stating plainly, since it is the second time in this project the same shape of error has appeared: I had evidence for one claim (the invariant is load-bearing) and spent it on a different one (the implementation is load-bearing).

issues.title: CacheGuard and StrategyGuard still rethrow a foreign CancellationException
issues.body:
`engine/CacheGuard.kt:43` and `engine/StrategyGuard.kt:32` both do:

```kotlin
catch (e: CancellationException) { throw e }
catch (e: Exception) { ...; fallback }
```

That is the pattern #53 established as wrong. `ensureActive()` throws only when *this* job is cancelled; a blanket rethrow cannot tell our cancellation from one raised inside the code being guarded. `ProviderChain`, `DefaultEnrichmentEngine`, `DeezerProvider` and `ITunesProvider` were all moved to `ensureActive()` during #53. These two were not — they predate it and were not revisited, so the codebase now carries both patterns.

The failure this allows: both guards wrap **consumer-implementable** interfaces — `EnrichmentCache` and the `ResultMerger`/`CompositeSynthesizer` extension points — which is the entire reason the guards exist. A consumer whose `RoomEnrichmentCache` subclass or custom merger uses its own `withTimeout` raises a `TimeoutCancellationException` on expiry. That is a `CancellationException`, so the guard rethrows it instead of degrading, and it escapes `enrich()`. The caller sees the engine as cancelled when nothing of ours was cancelled and the cache was merely slow — exactly the foreign-cancellation direction #53 fixed everywhere else.

`CacheGuard`s KDoc argues the rethrow is safe because "none of the current call sites sit inside `enrich()`s `withTimeout` block". That reasoning is about *our* cancellation reaching the guard. It does not address a cancellation originating inside the guarded block, which is the case that matters here.

Fix: replace both with the `ensureActive()` form, and pin it the way #53 did — a test with a guarded block that cancels via its own `withTimeout`, asserting `enrich()` completes and the type degrades rather than the whole call failing.

issues.title: ./check passes on a tree containing merge-conflict markers
issues.body:
Observed while rebasing during #58: `ARCHITECTURE.md` had unresolved conflict markers (`<<<<<<<`, `=======`, `>>>>>>>`) in the working tree, and `./check` ran to completion and printed **All checks passed**.

Nothing in the gate looks for them. ktlint and detekt only see Kotlin; ruff, mypy and shellcheck only see Python and shell; the convention rules only scan `*/src/main/**/*.kt`. Markdown, YAML, `.gradle.kts` and JSON are unexamined, so a half-finished merge in any of them passes.

`git diff --check` reports conflict markers as well as whitespace errors, and is already listed in the verification steps for this work — it is simply not in `./check`. One line, no new dependency:

```sh
git diff --check
```

Two things to decide when doing it:

- **Where.** It belongs above the `--fast` exit: it costs milliseconds and catches a state that makes everything below it meaningless.
- **What it covers.** `git diff --check` inspects tracked, unstaged changes. Staged content needs `git diff --cached --check`, and a fully committed conflict marker needs a grep over the tree. The cheap version catches the case that actually happens — a resolve that was never finished — and the limit should be written down rather than implied.

Low priority because a conflicted tree is usually loud for other reasons. Filed because it is the same shape as every other defect in this batch: a check reporting success while looking at nothing relevant.

issues.title: Collapse dev and main into one protected branch
issues.body:
The protection is on the branch that needs it least.

Measured from the live API:

| Branch | Role | Ruleset |
|---|---|---|
| `dev` | **default**, takes every change | `deletion`, `non_fast_forward` only |
| `main` | release merges only | `deletion`, `non_fast_forward`, `pull_request`, `required_status_checks` |

Five PRs merged on 2026-07-23/24 went into an unprotected branch. Nothing forced CI green; it was checked by hand each time.

What blocked protecting `dev` is the reason to delete it rather than protect it: `release.yml` fast-forwards with `git push origin main:dev`, which a `pull_request` rule rejects, and `github-actions[bot]` has no bypass. One branch removes the fast-forward entirely rather than carving an exception for it.

## Target

`main` as default, integration and release branch. Ruleset: pull request required (0 approvals), strict `build` + `demo-canary`, linear history, **squash-only**, restrict deletion, block force-push, **no bypass actors**. Repository: `allow_merge_commit: false`, `allow_rebase_merge: false`, `delete_branch_on_merge: true`.

Squash-only resolves the merge-method collision. The release PR no longer joins two permanent histories, so it gains nothing from a merge commit; epic consolidation squashes too, with the per-child history living in its PR.

## `release-readiness` is deleted, not retargeted

Its `base_ref == 'main'` condition becomes true on every ordinary PR after the collapse, so it would run rather than hang — but it should go regardless. It was added by #35 when publication was tag-triggered, so a version mismatch could only surface after an immutable tag existed, costing a delete-and-re-push. `release.yml` now asserts versions at line 81 and pushes the tag at line 218 — last, after publishing — so the mismatch already fails cheaply before any tag exists.

## Release flow afterwards

**Prepare release** pushes a `release/x.y.z` branch (refusing to overwrite an existing one) and prints a compare URL. A human opens and squash-merges the PR. Then dispatch **Release** from `main`.

**Merge freeze between those two steps.** `workflow_dispatch` pins `GITHUB_SHA` to the branch tip at dispatch time, so a PR landing in that window would release the wrong tree. Note the squash SHA, dispatch, confirm the run is on it, then merges resume.

No PAT, no GitHub App, no `pull-requests: write`, no bypass actor. A `GITHUB_TOKEN`-opened PR would also create approval-required runs, so bot-opening it saves a click and costs an approval.

## Also caught

`.github/dependabot.yml` targeted `dev`; `ARCHITECTURE.md` and `ROADMAP.md` carried stale `dev` and `api-drift` text; local `origin/HEAD` still points at `main`.

`origin/main` is an ancestor of `origin/dev`, 7 commits behind, so no reconciliation is needed, and there are zero open PRs — the cheapest moment to do this.

## Rehearsal, honestly bounded

`release.yml`'s `stage` mode proves dispatch-from-`main`, credentials, signing, upload and Central acceptance. It does **not** prove the release-branch push, the PR flow, version/README agreement (stage skips those), tag availability, tagging, the GitHub Release, JitPack, or the merge-to-dispatch race. The protected-PR flow is exercised by the migration PR itself.
comments:
Resolved by PR #69 (`Closes #68`), squash-merged as `bb3fd66` under merge `3db8f49` on 2026-07-23.

Verified each target against the live repo:

- **`main` is default** — `default_branch: main`; local `origin/HEAD → main`.
- **`dev` deleted** — remote branches are `main` (+ in-flight feature branches) only.
- **Protected ruleset `main protection`** (active, target `refs/heads/main`): `pull_request` (0 approvals), `required_status_checks` strict with `build` + `demo-canary`, `required_linear_history`, squash-only (`allowed_merge_methods: [squash]`), `deletion` + `non_fast_forward` rules, **`bypass_actors: []`**.
- **Repo merge settings** — `allow_merge_commit: false`, `allow_rebase_merge: false`, `allow_squash_merge: true`, `delete_branch_on_merge: true`.
- **`release-readiness` gate deleted** — no reference anywhere under `.github/`; no such workflow.
- **`.github/dependabot.yml` retargeted** — no `target-branch:`, so it follows the sole default branch (`main`), with a comment saying exactly that.
- **Stale `dev`/`api-drift` text** — no `dev`-branch references remain in `ARCHITECTURE.md` or `ROADMAP.md`; the two remaining `api-drift` mentions in `ROADMAP.md` are correct historical changelog entries (recording that `api-drift.yml` was deleted), not stale process text.

All acceptance-shaped targets landed. Closing as completed.

issues.title: EnrichmentLogger is consumer-implementable and called unguarded inside every engine guard
issues.body:
`EnrichmentLogger` is public and consumer-implementable, and every guard in the engine calls it **from inside the guard, where a throw escapes the very protection the guard is there to provide**:

- `engine/CacheGuard.kt:54` — `logger.warn(...)` inside the catch, between `ensureActive()` and returning the fallback
- `engine/StrategyGuard.kt:41` — same, inside the catch before building the `Error`
- `engine/ProviderChain.kt:56,60` — `logger.debug(...)` on the RateLimited and Error branches of the result `when`, after the try/catch and `ensureActive()` — not in a catch, but equally unguarded inside the `async`, so a throw there propagates out through `awaitAll()`

So a consumer logger that throws defeats the guard that was catching for it. The cache guard exists precisely so a broken `EnrichmentCache` degrades to a miss rather than failing `enrich()` — but if the log line describing that degradation throws, `enrich()` fails anyway, and now with an exception that names the logger rather than the cache.

This is the same defect class as #22 (throwing cache), #28 (throwing merger) and #61 (foreign cancellation in both guards): **a consumer-implementable interface reached without a guard.** `CLAUDE.md` names three such interfaces and says each needs one. `EnrichmentLogger` is the fourth and was never counted, because it is invoked from inside the guards rather than from the enrichment path.

Failure this allows: a consumer supplies a logger that writes to a file, a crash reporter, or an Android `Log` wrapper. Disk full, a closed handle, or an SDK not yet initialised throws — and a cache miss, which the engine is designed to absorb silently, becomes a failed `enrich()`.

Worth deciding rather than assuming:

1. Whether logging failures should be swallowed outright (a logger has no result to degrade to, so `runCatching {}.getOrNull()` is likely the whole fix), or
2. whether `EnrichmentLogger` should be documented as \"must not throw\" and left unguarded, which is a real option for an interface this trivial — but then say so in its KDoc, because nothing currently does.

Note the cancellation question is already settled above the logger call in both guards: `ensureActive()` runs first, so a swallow here cannot eat a cancellation. Any fix should keep that ordering.

Found while fixing #61; not fixed there to keep that change to one invariant.
comments:
## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement (defensive hardening — same defect class as #22, #28, #61)
**Summary:** `EnrichmentLogger` is a public, consumer-implementable interface invoked from inside the guards' `catch` blocks; a logger that throws re-defeats the guard that was catching for it and fails `enrich()`.

**Current behavior:**
- `EnrichmentLogger` is public (confirmed in `api/musicmeta-core.api` — `public abstract interface class ...EnrichmentLogger`), wired via `EnrichmentEngine.Builder.logger(...)`, default `EnrichmentLogger.NoOp`. Its KDoc says nothing about throwing.
- In `CacheGuard.runGuarded`, the `catch (e: Exception)` branch calls `logger.warn(...)` before returning the fallback. If that call throws, the exception escapes the guard — and since `guardedCacheRead`/`guardedCacheWrite` are the cache guard, nothing above re-catches, so `enrich()` fails. The cache guard exists precisely so a broken cache degrades to a miss; a throwing log line about that degradation fails `enrich()` anyway.
- In `StrategyGuard.guardedStrategy`, the `catch (e: Exception)` branch calls `logger.warn(...)` before building the `Error`; a throw there escapes for that type.
- In `ProviderChain`, `logger.debug(...)` is called on the `RateLimited` and `Error` result branches. Note these sit on the `when(result)` dispatch **after** `ensureActive()`, not literally inside the `catch` — but a throwing logger there still escapes the fanned-out `async` and fails the type. (The issue title's "inside every guard's catch block" is exact for the two guards, approximate for ProviderChain.)

This is the invariant CLAUDE.md states for this class: *every consumer-implementable interface reached from `enrich()` needs a guard; a throwing consumer degrades, never fails `enrich()`.* `EnrichmentLogger` is the interface that was never counted, because it is called from inside the other guards rather than from the enrichment path.

**Desired behavior:**
A consumer `EnrichmentLogger` whose `debug`/`warn` throws must not fail `enrich()`. The engine degrades exactly as if the log line had succeeded (cache still misses to a provider round-trip; strategy still reports its `Error`; provider result still dispatches).

**Key interfaces:**
- `EnrichmentLogger.debug(tag, message)` / `warn(tag, message, throwable)` — the two call surfaces that can throw.
- `CacheGuard.runGuarded`, `StrategyGuard.guardedStrategy`, `ProviderChain` result-dispatch — the call sites.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] A consumer logger that throws from `debug`/`warn` does not cause `enrich()` (or an individual type's resolution) to fail — verified by a test with a throwing fake logger, mirroring `EnrichCacheFailureTest` / `EnrichStrategyFailureTest`.
- [ ] The chosen resolution is applied consistently at all three sites (both guards + ProviderChain), not just the path the title names.
- [ ] No regression in the cancellation invariant: whatever wraps the logger call must not swallow *this job's* cancellation. Quoting CLAUDE.md pitfall 2 — "`ensureActive()` throws only when *this* job is cancelled." A `runCatching {}` around a non-suspend `logger.warn` cannot eat a cancellation, but the ordering (cancellation settled before the logger call) must be preserved.
- [ ] If Option B is chosen, `EnrichmentLogger`'s KDoc states the must-not-throw contract (nothing currently does).

**Out of scope:**
- The #61 cancellation fix itself (see below — that is PR #70, in flight).
- Changing the logger interface signature or the `NoOp` default.

**References (current code at time of triage — may shift):**
- `engine/CacheGuard.kt` — `logger.warn` in the `catch (e: Exception)` branch of `runGuarded`.
- `engine/StrategyGuard.kt` — `logger.warn` in the `catch (e: Exception)` branch of `guardedStrategy`.
- `engine/ProviderChain.kt` — `logger.debug` on the RateLimited/Error branches, after `ensureActive()`.
- `EnrichmentLogger.kt` — public interface, no must-not-throw KDoc.
- `api/musicmeta-core.api` — confirms public visibility.
- Sibling guards: #22 (throwing cache), #28 (throwing merger), #61 (foreign cancellation).

**Why this needs a human:**
Two unresolved decisions, neither of which triage can make for the maintainer.

1. **The body poses Option A vs Option B and no one has picked.** Option A: swallow logging failures outright (a logger has no result to degrade to, so `runCatching {}.getOrNull()` around each call is likely the whole fix). Option B: document `EnrichmentLogger` as "must not throw" in its KDoc and leave it unguarded — a defensible choice for an interface this trivial. This is the maintainer's contract call, not an implementer's.

2. **It collides with in-flight work.** PR #70 (`core/61` → `main`, open, unmerged) rewrites the exact `catch` blocks in both `CacheGuard` and `StrategyGuard` to replace the blanket `catch (CancellationException) { throw e }` with `ensureActive()`. On `main` today those guards still use the blanket rethrow — so this issue's premise that "`ensureActive()` runs first" describes the *post-#70* state, not current `main`. The clean fix for #71 belongs on top of #70, or #70's scope could absorb it. Sequencing/merge order is a design call for the maintainer.
## Triage re-verification (2026-07-26) — one blocker has cleared

The defect is unchanged on `docs/claude-md-pointers`: `EnrichmentLogger` is still public and
consumer-supplied, and it is still called unguarded at all three sites —
`CacheGuard.kt:54` (`logger.warn` in the `catch`), `StrategyGuard.kt:41` (`logger.warn` in the
`catch`), and `ProviderChain.kt:58,63` (`logger.debug` on the `RateLimited`/`Error` branches).

**The in-flight collision named under "Why this needs a human" is gone.** PR #70 merged as bb2bfa6
("fix(engine): settle cancellation in CacheGuard and StrategyGuard with `ensureActive()`"), so both
guards are already on the `ensureActive()` shape on `main`. The issue body's premise that
`ensureActive()` runs before the logger call now describes current `main`, not a future state, and
there is nothing left to sequence behind.

That leaves **exactly one** open item, and it is still a human call: **Option A vs Option B.**
Swallow logging failures (`runCatching { }` around each of the three call sites — likely the whole
fix), or declare `EnrichmentLogger` "must not throw" in its KDoc and leave it unguarded, on the
grounds that the interface is trivial enough to hold consumers to it. `CLAUDE.md`'s rule — every
consumer-implementable interface reached from `enrich()` degrades rather than fails — argues for A;
the interface's triviality argues for B. Neither is triage's decision.

Once that is picked the work is small: three wrapped call sites and one test with a throwing fake
logger, mirroring `EnrichCacheFailureTest` / `EnrichStrategyFailureTest`.

Stays `ready-for-human`, on the contract question alone.

issues.title: Step 5: one measured context experiment — a single path-scoped .claude/rules/providers.md, kept only if it moves the numbers
issues.body:
One measured context experiment: a single path-scoped `.claude/rules/providers.md`, kept only if it moves the numbers.

## Why

The agent-facing docs have one concrete routing defect: **`CLAUDE.md` never links `docs/providers/` at all.** 1,735 lines of usable per-provider reference (11 files, 1:1 with the 11 provider packages) have no inbound link from the one document read every session, so an agent that greps its way to `LrclibApi.kt` never finds the spec for it.

This is deliberately the smallest possible version. Two reasons it is not bigger:

- **Genre mismatch.** A colocated per-provider rules file would want the module's *own business rules*. Our `docs/providers/*.md` is mostly the *third party's API reference* — endpoints, JSON shapes, auth, rate limits. Related, not the same; merging them into one colocated file fuses two different artifacts. → colocation is **Dead**, not deferred.
- **Drift.** `docs/providers/README.md` already restates values the code owns (the MusicBrainz row says `1100ms`, which lives in `RateLimiter(1100)` in `Builder.withDefaultProviders()`). Moving docs nearer the code relocates that rot into higher-traffic territory; it does not fix it.

## What to do

1. Add **one** path-scoped `.claude/rules/providers.md` with `paths:` frontmatter covering `provider/<name>/`. **Two requirements only:**
   - read the matching `docs/providers/<name>.md` before touching a provider;
   - test parsing against a fixture copied from a real API response.
2. Add the missing one-line pointer to `docs/providers/` from `CLAUDE.md` (the actual defect — cheap, gets most of the value even if the rule is later deleted).
3. **Do not** move or relocate the provider documents, and **do not** create colocated `feature_definition.md` files. The defect is routing, not location.

## Measurement (the point of the experiment)

Compare provider tasks carrying the rule against a ten-task baseline — the four numbers recorded in every PR body: first-pass gate result, agent retries, human corrections, supervision minutes.

**If corrections do not drop, delete the rule.** A path-scoped rule that does not move the numbers is noise every provider task pays for.

## Depends on

- A ten-task baseline must exist first: ten tasks with the four numbers recorded in their PR bodies. Without it there is nothing to compare against.

## Exit criteria

- [ ] `.claude/rules/providers.md` added (two requirements, path-scoped) **or** a written, dated decision not to.
- [ ] `CLAUDE.md` links `docs/providers/` (kept regardless of the rule's fate).
- [ ] Provider tasks measured against the ten-task baseline.
- [ ] The rule has either earned its place (corrections dropped) or been removed — the next proposed harness change can cite a number instead of a feeling.

## Explicitly out of scope (Dead — not deferred)

Colocated `feature_definition.md`, mass provider-doc relocation, `specs/`, `docs/decisions/`. Matching documented rate limits against `RateLimiter(...)` literals is a real parser and deserves its own separate issue.

issues.title: MusicBrainz sheds load with 503, which the retry ladder does not retry
issues.body:
`DefaultHttpClient` has a complete retry ladder — bounded attempts, `Retry-After` honoured,
exponential backoff with jitter, and a deadline-aware refusal to sleep past the enclosing
`enrich()` budget. It fires for exactly one condition: `HttpResult.RateLimited`, which only a
**429** produces.

MusicBrainz does not shed load with 429. It sheds with **503**, carrying the same `Retry-After` and
`X-RateLimit-*` headers a 429 would. A 503 maps to `HttpResult.ServerError`, which the retry loop
returns unretried on the first attempt. So the mechanism built for throttling never runs against
the throttling signal our highest-traffic provider actually sends.

### Impact

Availability, not correctness. A `ServerError` still becomes a thrown `IOException` →
`ErrorKind.NETWORK` → a circuit-breaker *failure*, so a shed request is never mistaken for
`NotFound`. The cost is that a single shed response fails a lookup one retry a second later would
have answered.

### Evidence

Probed live 2026-08-09, 10 requests spaced 1.2s — under MusicBrainz's documented 1 req/s ceiling,
so this is not us exceeding our own budget:

```
200 200 200 200 200 200 503 200 200 200
```

The shed response's headers:

```
HTTP/2 503
retry-after: 0
x-ratelimit-limit: 15
x-ratelimit-remaining: 14
x-ratelimit-reset: 1786276103
x-ratelimit-zone: global
```

`x-ratelimit-zone: global` with `remaining: 14` says MusicBrainz's search cluster sheds against a
*global* budget — no amount of client-side pacing prevents it.

Surfaced by scheduled run
[31297181005](https://github.com/famesjranko/musicmeta/actions/runs/31297181005), which failed on
both the first attempt and the workflow's built-in retry. The drift alarm was a false positive; this
was underneath it.

### Fix

Retry **502, 503 and 504** on the existing ladder. 500 and 501 stay terminal — 500 is "something
broke" with no implication that a retry helps, and 501 never will be. A closed list of three codes,
not a `500..599` range test, which would silently absorb every future 5xx.

Contained inside `DefaultHttpClient`: `ServerError` cannot gain a `Retry-After` field without
breaking `copy()` for every consumer, so the header travels in a private carrier. Empty `api/*.api`
diff, ships as a patch.
comments:
Closing: filed in error. This repo's issue tracker is `.scratch/`, per `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` — the work is tracked there as `http-transient-retry/issues/01-retry-503.md` and ships as PR #156, which no longer references this issue.

Nothing here is withdrawn: MusicBrainz does shed with 503, and the fix is landing. Only the tracking location was wrong.

issues.title: Split the 28-package Dependabot gradle bump (#226) into landable PRs
issues.body:
Dependabot opened #226 bumping 28 packages in the `gradle` group as one PR. It cannot land as one PR, and the CI failure it produced measures almost nothing.

## Why it can't land as-is

Both jobs (`build`, `demo-canary`) fail at Gradle **configuration** time, before a single source file is compiled:

```
An exception occurred applying plugin request [id: 'org.jetbrains.kotlin.android', version: '2.4.10']
> Failed to apply plugin 'org.jetbrains.kotlin.android'
  The 'org.jetbrains.kotlin.android' plugin is no longer required for Kotlin support since AGP 9.0.
  Solution: Remove the 'org.jetbrains.kotlin.android' plugin from this project's build file:
            musicmeta-android/build.gradle.kts.
  See https://kotl.in/gradle/agp-built-in-kotlin
```

Source: run 32159789540, jobs 95785643775 and 95785643601.

`musicmeta-android/build.gradle.kts:6` applies `alias(libs.plugins.kotlin.android)`. AGP 9.3.1 ships built-in Kotlin and makes the standalone plugin a hard error. That is a build-model migration, not a version bump.

Because configuration dies first, **nothing in that run tells us anything** about OkHttp 5, Room 2.8, Kotlin 2.4, or kotlinx-serialization 1.11 source or binary compatibility. Those are unmeasured, not passing.

## Why it can't land as one PR even once it configures

Three of the bumps land on rules in `CLAUDE.md` that a green build does not check:

- **OkHttp 4.12 -> 5.4.0** is a major bump of a dependency the `musicmeta-okhttp` adapter puts on every consumer's classpath. Breaking, needs a `### Breaking Changes` entry in `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Room 2.6.1 -> 2.8.4** touches the schema path. `musicmeta-android/src/androidTest/` is run by nothing — not `check`, not CI — so a migration reaches a release proved only against Robolectric's SQLite. Already the gate on 0.11.0.
- **kotlinx-serialization 1.7.3 -> 1.11.0** can change the encoding of a `@Serializable` cache type. No `api/*.api` line moves, and the round-trip tests encode and decode with the same tree, so they cannot see a payload a consumer already persisted becoming unreadable. That is what v0.4.0 did.

## Plan

Close #226. Land the split in the child issues below, in order. Each child is one PR that is green on its own, so a revert is a revert of one thing.

The children are ordered by risk, lowest first, and 02 blocks 03/04/05 — those bumps cannot even be evaluated until the build configures again.
comments: State sync (2026-08-25): the grouped bump's successor #235 is closed, and .github/dependabot.yml now keeps majors out of the shared weekly group (#268) — future dependabot PRs arrive shaped like stages 1–5 (#228–#232) instead of as one group. Failure evidence for stage 2 captured from #235's CI: AGP 9 refuses `org.jetbrains.kotlin.android` (built-in Kotlin, musicmeta-android/build.gradle.kts:4).

Closed with the dependency policy change in #279. The premise — split the grouped bump into landable PRs — no longer holds: dependencies a consumer inherits are not chased at all now, so there is nothing to split. Full text archived at .scratch/dependency-majors/gh-227.md.

issues.title: deps 2/5: Gradle 9 + AGP 9 + Kotlin 2.4 + KSP — includes the AGP built-in Kotlin migration
issues.body:
**Parent:** the #226 split.
**Blocks:** the OkHttp, Room, and core-runtime children — none of them can be evaluated until the build configures again.

The toolchain moves as one unit because AGP, Kotlin, and KSP are version-locked to each other.

| Package | From | To |
|---|---|---|
| gradle-wrapper | 8.13 | 9.7.0 |
| `com.android.library` (AGP) | 8.7.3 | 9.3.1 |
| `org.jetbrains.kotlin.{android,jvm,plugin.serialization}` | 2.1.0 | 2.4.10 |
| `com.google.devtools.ksp` | 2.1.0-1.0.29 | 2.3.11 |
| `com.google.dagger:hilt-*` | 2.54 | 2.60.1 |
| `androidx.hilt:hilt-{work,compiler}` | 1.2.0 | 1.4.0 |
| `com.vanniktech.maven.publish` | 0.30.0 | 0.37.0 |

## The known blocker

`musicmeta-android/build.gradle.kts:6` applies `alias(libs.plugins.kotlin.android)`. Under AGP 9 that is a hard error — Kotlin is built in. Removing the line is the start of the migration, not the end: AGP built-in Kotlin moves where `kotlinOptions` / jvm toolchain / KSP wiring are declared. See https://kotl.in/gradle/agp-built-in-kotlin.

Expect the next configuration error after that one, and compile errors after that. Budget accordingly.

## Also in scope

- **Gradle 9** removes long-deprecated APIs. `scripts/checks/` and any convention plugin need re-reading, not just the module build files.
- **vanniktech 0.30 -> 0.37** owns publication. A change here is invisible until a release goes out wrong. Verify the generated POM and the `AndroidSingleVariantLibrary` config still produce the same coordinates, packaging, and dependency scopes.
- **`binary-compatibility-validator` and `detekt`** are pinned separately and may not be compatible with Gradle 9 / Kotlin 2.4. If either has to move, say so here rather than folding it in silently.
- **ktlint** is pinned in three places that must agree (`libs.versions.toml`, `scripts/format-on-write.sh`, `scripts/bootstrap.sh` `KTLINT_SHA256`). Do not move it unless Gradle 9 forces it.

## Done when

`make check` is green, `demo-canary` is green, and `api/*.api` is unchanged — a toolchain bump that moves an ABI line is a finding, not a bump. Kotlin 2.4 may change generated JVM descriptors; if a line moves, explain which and why before dumping.
comments: Closed with the dependency policy change in #279. The toolchain migration is still owed — it is now tracked in .scratch/dependency-majors/ rather than here, and the monthly build-tooling PR is what will keep surfacing it. Full text archived at .scratch/dependency-majors/gh-229.md.

issues.title: deps 3/5: OkHttp 4.12 -> 5.4.0 — consumer-visible transitive break
issues.body:
**Parent:** the #226 split.
**Blocked by:** the toolchain child.

| Package | From | To |
|---|---|---|
| `com.squareup.okhttp3:okhttp` | 4.12.0 | 5.4.0 |
| `com.squareup.okhttp3:mockwebserver` | 4.12.0 | 5.4.0 |

## Why this is its own PR

`musicmeta-okhttp` exists to bring OkHttp. The dependency is on every consumer's classpath, so a major bump is a consumer-visible break whether or not our own `api/*.api` moves — a consumer on OkHttp 4 who upgrades gets a runtime conflict we caused.

Under the compatibility rule this needs, before merge:
- a `### Breaking Changes` heading in `CHANGELOG.md`, and
- the break flagged to the maintainer explicitly, not just written down.

## Watch for

- **OkHttp 5 changed `MediaType`, `Headers`, and several Kotlin properties-vs-functions**, and moved `mockwebserver` artifact coordinates in some configurations. Check the coordinate before assuming the version bump alone is enough.
- **Timeout, cancellation, and interceptor semantics** are the exact area `docs/pitfalls.md` warns about. Any behaviour change in how a cancelled call surfaces must be checked against the `Error`/`NotFound` classification, not assumed inert.
- The retry ladder and breaker sit on top of this transport. Re-read `docs/pitfalls.md` - "Transport and provider state" before touching it.

## Done when

`make check` is green, the `CHANGELOG.md` breaking entry exists, and the timeout/cancellation tests were watched fail against a deliberate mutation — not merely seen green.
comments: Closed with the dependency policy change in #279. OkHttp 5 is now a bump we make for a reason, not one we accept from a robot — and Gradle's highest-wins resolution means staying on 4.12 costs consumers nothing while publishing 5.x forces it on them. issues.title: deps 5/5: coroutines + kotlinx-serialization 1.11 — cache payload compatibility
issues.body:
**Parent:** the #226 split.
**Blocked by:** the toolchain child.

| Package | From | To |
|---|---|---|
| `org.jetbrains.kotlinx:kotlinx-serialization-json` | 1.7.3 | 1.11.0 |
| `org.jetbrains.kotlinx:kotlinx-coroutines-{core,android,test}` | 1.9.0 | 1.11.0 |

## Why this is its own PR

Both are `musicmeta-core` dependencies, so both reach every consumer transitively and cannot be withdrawn without a break.

The serialization bump is the dangerous half. A `@Serializable` cache type is a compatibility surface no gate reads:
- it moves no `api/*.api` line, and
- the round-trip tests encode and decode with the same tree, so they cannot see a payload a consumer **already persisted** becoming unreadable.

That is exactly v0.4.0, which broke every Room cache entry.

## Required before merge

- **A decode-old-payload test.** Take a JSON string captured under 1.7.3, commit it as a fixture, and decode it with 1.11.0. A fixture must predate the change it is evidence for, so capture it from the current `main`, not from the bumped branch.
- If the encoding did change: treat it as a break under the compatibility rule, and ask the maintainer about a cache-clear note.

## Watch for

- kotlinx-serialization 1.8+ changed defaults around `explicitNulls`, sealed-class discriminators, and `JsonNamingStrategy` handling in ways that alter output for some shapes.
- coroutines 1.10/1.11 tightened `runTest` and cancellation behaviour. `docs/pitfalls.md` - "Errors, cancellation, and timeouts" is the contract that must not move.

## Done when

`make check` is green and the old-payload decode test exists, was watched fail (mutate the fixture, confirm red), and passes.
